sources.title: Design trends overview for 2026
sources.notes: Trend directions: conversational interfaces, adaptive personalisation, functional motion, spatial interfaces, design tokens, inclusive design.

sources.title: Interface design trend roundup for 2026
sources.notes: Trend directions: personalised interfaces, modular grid layouts, accessibility-first systems, voice and multimodal input, purposeful micro-interactions.

sources.title: Frontend design patterns overview
sources.notes: Component-driven structure, grid for page structure and flexible rows for components, container queries, fluid type, dark theme via variables.

sources.title: Component library listing
sources.notes: Shortlist of free, maintained component libraries by use case.

sources.title: Responsive landing page construction
sources.notes: Fluid type with clamp, grid with auto-fit and minmax, mobile-first breakpoints.

sources.title: Commerce landing page practices
sources.notes: Trust elements, clear calls to action, multiple product views, mobile-first layout.

sources.title: October 2026 component release: step trace and code block
sources.notes: New primitives: a step-trace list for automated task runs (icon, title, description, status per line; running, error, pending states; expandable and nested lines) and a code block for code, terminal output, logs, and diffs (header with actions, line numbers, wrapping, highlighted lines).

sources.title: Overlay composition update: trigger wrappers, sheet positions, dialog parts
sources.notes: Overlay pattern: trigger wrapper manages the interaction, a control opens it, and the component renders the content. Sheets choose the opening edge by position; drawers and modals are unified under sheet and dialog with header, body, footer, and close parts.

sources.title: Streaming interface rendering: 1.0 release notes and version analysis
sources.notes: Interface programs composed from registered components render progressively as they stream; the registered set controls what can appear; syntax instructions must match the client runtime version; cut-off streams render blank rather than a partial tree.

sources.title: October 2026 release: drag-and-drop form builder component
sources.notes: New web component: a drag-and-drop form designer with more than 20 built-in form components, available across multiple web frameworks. Pattern: a field palette feeds a canvas; settings sit beside the selected field; a live preview precedes saving.

sources.title: App UI kit changelog: October 2026 carousel focus and layering fixes
sources.notes: A carousel scroll button returns focus to the pressed button after scrolling completes; paging never moves keyboard focus outside the carousel; styles use cascade layers where the browser supports them with a fallback otherwise.

sources.title: October 2026 component release: Markdown content block
sources.notes: New reporting component for rendering Markdown content (headers, lists, tables, images, links, code blocks) with CommonMark 0.31.2 and GFM support; content is editable directly in the component editor.

sources.title: October 2026 changelog: dual-style App UI blocks
sources.notes: Component library update shipping its App UI block set in two complete styles: a precise monochrome default and a roomy, warm, tactile variant (larger controls and rows, raised tiles, inset fields). Styles switch from the theme panel; every block keeps the same layout, data, states, keyboard handling, and motion; blocks install per style with a suffixed name.

sources.title: Web design trend roundup: modular tile layouts and accessibility guardrails
sources.notes: Modular tile (bento) layouts and barely-there styling: failure modes include poor small-screen collapse and grid reordering breaking reading order for screen readers and keyboard focus; recommended fix is to write the markup in priority order and use named grid areas to rearrange tiles at breakpoints; thin lightweight text risks contrast failures.

sources.title: Design-system motion specification
sources.notes: Motion values: 115/165/250 ms durations, responsive/sticky/expressive easing curves, scale for incoming items, slide for structural moves, no flash beyond three per second, reduced-motion honoured, motion tokens for custom components.

sources.title: Design-system release notes, October 2026
sources.notes: New combobox guidance (design only), refreshed guidance for back button, back-to-top, in-page navigation, links, critical and page alerts, loading indicator, and search box; hotfix correcting broken global styles.

sources.title: Skeleton component changelog v18.0.0
sources.notes: Breaking theme change (default/invert only); chart placeholders moved to masks with theme-dependent colours.

sources.title: Standards-body design system update, September 2026
sources.notes: CSS reset replaced, typography rebuilt around a new type scale, simplified space management, wrapper elements removed to simplify page markup.

sources.title: Agent-to-UI interface playbook
sources.notes: Streaming-rendered interfaces in conversational surfaces; agent-mediated purchase pattern; reversibility-tiered approval gates (free/confirm/gate); calibrated confidence states with source citations.

sources.title: Voice interface design guide, 2026
sources.notes: Voice as a first-class control surface: one-breath steps with per-step confirmation, about three spoken options at a time, repair paths asking only for the missing piece, barge-in support, multimodal pairing of voice summary with screen detail.

sources.title: Ecommerce checkout optimisation guide, 2026
sources.notes: Checkout variants: one-page for low-cost impulse purchases, multi-step with total step count for high-cost purchases; running order total visible, instalment options under the total, guest and wallet-accelerated checkout, explicit payment-retry states.

sources.title: Multi-surface app guide
sources.notes: Anticipatory design across surfaces: task continuity (start on watch, continue on phone, finish in spatial); navigation migrates bottom bar to side rail; components morph from terse to detailed; companion-app pattern for spatial sessions.

sources.title: Foldable app UI considerations
sources.notes: Canonical foldable layouts (list-detail, supporting pane, feed); design for postures (closed, half-open, fully open, tent); fold treated as a seam; warm transitions with exact scroll and focus restoration; critical elements kept away from the hinge.

sources.title: Micro-interaction examples and skeleton screens
sources.notes: Skeleton screens replace spinners; stream long output progressively; name the steps of longer operations; optimistic updates with quiet revert on failure; inline validation on blur.

sources.title: UI and UX trends shaping 2026
sources.notes: Post-dashboard narrative interfaces (synthesis, what-changed reports); adaptive interfaces reordering in real time; calm interfaces; ultra-contextual navigation that shrinks itself.

sources.title: UI and UX design trends (slug reads 2025, content covers 2026)
sources.notes: Conversational layer beside a conventional interface: route each request to words, to the right screen, or to both; the handoff is the design challenge.

sources.title: Wearable app complete guide
sources.notes: Glance layouts: 3-5 second interactions, single most important datum, no scrolling, rotational input as primary scroll, separate ambient and active display states.

sources.title: SaaS onboarding UX patterns
sources.notes: Onboarding mechanics: interactive checklists with progress indicators, contextual micro-learning, value-first signup, personalisation routing, per-area confirmations.

sources.title: Mixing WebGL and the DOM in a modular UI library
sources.notes: Cursor-reactive media effects (ripple, pixel blocks, lens dispersion) layered over images and video on one shared full-page canvas; real element kept in the DOM at zero opacity for accessibility; per-element opt-out of global effects; per-frame remeasurement only while a transform moves the element.

sources.title: Television interface design guide
sources.notes: Focus as the centre of the TV model; shelves of posters as the primary navigation structure; spoken queries preferred over step-through on-screen keyboards; legibility at room distance.

sources.title: Ten-foot user interface overview
sources.notes: Directional remote as primary input; grid arrangement so every item has a clear neighbour in each direction; larger type for distance; no pointer; viewing distance expressed in picture heights.

sources.title: Lessons from streaming platform design practice
sources.notes: Focus as the new tap; scaling-plus-colour focus indicators; simplified information architecture for remote navigation; complex flows handed to a second device via codes; ten-foot rule for type size.

sources.title: Voice menu accessibility patterns
sources.notes: Tapered prompts that grow more explanatory on silence; adjustable timeouts and speech speed as user settings; error recovery that offers human help rather than a harder menu; plain jargon-free terms.

sources.title: Voice interface design principles
sources.notes: Short responses; consistent interruption handling; diagnosis-led error recovery; signifiers for discoverability; structured alternatives for comparison-heavy tasks; confirmation before irreversible tool actions.

sources.title: Gesture-based UI design essentials
sources.notes: Small consistent gesture sets with one meaning per gesture; thresholds against accidental activation; immediate recognition feedback; spatial metaphors matching expectations; easy undo of accidental gestures.

sources.title: Accessible gesture interaction
sources.notes: Simple learnable gestures; consistent feedback; error guidance and recovery; ergonomic comfort for repeated use; alternative input methods for essential tasks.

sources.title: React component library release notes 2.14.0
sources.notes: New component set: a control for entering and removing collections of free-form values; a compact copy control for identifiers and values in dense interfaces; a dialog with responsive behaviour including mobile drawer support and dismissal handling.

sources.title: Empty-state design for usually-absent content
sources.notes: Three kinds of empty: nothing yet and expected, nothing because of a limit, nothing because of failure; each needs different wording and next step; model status explicitly instead of inferring from item count.

sources.title: Strategic value of empty states
sources.notes: Empty-state types: first-time experiences, natural empty states, search failures, system errors; messaging pivots on whether the user, the system, or the lack of data is responsible.

sources.title: Empty state as first-use guidance
sources.notes: An empty screen is the first screen every new account sees; four jobs: explain what belongs here, show the filled version, prompt exactly one action, and remove the fear of being wrong; distinguish genuinely blank, labelled sample data, and seeded setup; a filtered view that matches nothing is a different state from an empty collection.

sources.title: AI surface patterns: inline, agents, ambient
sources.notes: Three patterns beyond chatbots: inline AI as a verb on the existing surface, agents and copilots with human-in-the-loop confirmation, ambient OS-level assistance; voice affordances: live transcript, confidence state, obvious correction path.

sources.title: Onboarding default-state pitfalls
sources.notes: Wrong defaults act as silent errors; detect device language, prefill region with a correction affordance, no default for sensitive fields, explain why a field is asked, progressive disclosure one question at a time.

sources.title: Emerging web design trends for 2026
sources.notes: Emerging: machine-experience design - structure pages so automated agents read and complete tasks accurately; failure mode is markup order not matching visual order. Also notes barely-there UI restraint (single typeface, low-opacity hairlines, whitespace-based structure) and bento grids.

sources.title: Embedded touchscreen HMI product guidelines
sources.notes: Anti-reflection and anti-glare treatments preserve legibility in bright environments; anti-fingerprint coatings lower finger friction and ease cleaning; readability decisions start at the lens and glass layer, weighing cost against optical clarity.

sources.title: Touchscreen HMI best-practice guide
sources.notes: Prefer single touch for consistency across heterogeneous screens; minimise movement-dependent controls such as swipes and sliders; do not use touchscreens for momentary jog controls since values can get stuck; avoid gesture navigation and on-screen keyboards on resistive screens.

sources.title: Industrial display panels: a practical guide for embedded HMI
sources.notes: Outdoor and high-ambient panels commonly need 800-1500+ nits, paired with reflection control; capacitive suits modern multi-touch, resistive suits gloves, stylus, and harsh conditions; common industrial panels run 7-10 in at 1024x600 to 1280x800.

sources.title: E-paper display module selection guide
sources.notes: E-paper refreshes on the order of seconds with a visible full-refresh flash: unsuitable for video, moving cursors, or fast charts; partial refresh is a controller capability to specify early; readable in sunlight with no backlight; small panels suit single-value readouts, large panels documents and drawings.

sources.title: Touch targets, gestures and interaction feedback
sources.notes: Discoverability cues: drag handles, peeking adjacent pages, chevrons, one-time contextual coach marks, redundant visible controls; progressive disclosure reveals swipe actions as the swipe begins; direction locking once movement passes a small threshold (about 8 px separates tap from drag; about 24 px begins revealing actions).

sources.title: Gestures and digital accessibility guidance
sources.notes: Functions operable by multipoint or path-based gestures must also be operable with a single pointer unless the gesture is essential; commit on the up-event and allow abort or undo; targets at least 44x44 CSS px; do not restrict content to a single input modality.

sources.title: Spatial information architecture for AR and VR
sources.notes: Three depth models: flat (one plane for dashboards), deep (nested rooms for guided focus), layered (near/mid/far for context plus detail); place primary actions closer for focal order via depth contrast; keep a home zone at body-centre height; use gaze rays with timeouts and audio beacons for off-screen targets.

sources.title: Spatial UI design tips and best practices
sources.notes: Content distance between about 1.25 m and 5 m: closer invades personal space and risks collisions, farther is hard to read; keep content in the central field of view and never fully obscure the environment; anchor animation and audio triggers to viewing distance.

sources.title: Voice agents: turn-taking and interruption design
sources.notes: Every conversational state needs its own timeout: re-prompt once on silence, then offer keypad input, then end politely; barge-in target around 300 ms from speech start to stopped output; backchannel words do not count as interruptions; set explicit loop limits with safe transfer or end.

sources.title: Agentic AI UX patterns
sources.notes: Rollback is first-class: one-click undo for every reversible agent action; failures state exactly what failed and why; partial completion shows per-step status, never presented as full success or failure; trust gradient: preview mode, then supervised, then autonomous only after repeated success.

sources.title: Design system update: approval workflows, citation cards, run recovery
sources.notes: An October 2026 design-system release for assistant-style interfaces added approval-workflow support so proposed agent actions are presented for human review, citation cards that place evidence beside system answers, and run recovery for interrupted multi-step tasks. The citation card is the substantive new primitive; approval handling is already covered in the agentic-ux trend note.

sources.title: Weekly Reading List October 19 2026
sources.notes: Reading list covering scroll-triggered animation as the missing piece for scrollytelling on the web; the substantive rule is that users relying on assistive technology such as screen readers must be considered — content revealed by scroll position must remain available to them rather than gated behind scroll alone.

sources.title: Design Trends That Will Influence Extensions in 2026
sources.notes: Design trends for browser extensions in 2026: the classic popup-centric model is giving way to the inline overlay — a floating panel anchored to the cursor or a page element, behaving as part of the page interface. Rules: anchor to cursor/element not the toolbar, show results next to their source, cheap dismissal returning focus to the anchor, web component with closed shadow root preferred over iframes for focus and keyboard reasons, handle shadow DOM/z-index/scroll on arbitrary host pages, size to content, full keyboard access.

sources.title: Validation gate for generated interface trees
sources.notes: Author-side gate: check a generated interface tree against the registered component set before rendering; invented components and unapproved form destinations are caught at authoring time; keep the check cheap enough to run on every tree.

sources.title: Design tools and UI component libraries for designers and developers, October 2026
sources.notes: Action-state grouping: one typed, accessible component that holds the visual states of an interface action (idle, loading, success) and transitions between them, removing scattered icon and label logic across the codebase.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Target Size: What Teams Should Test
sources.notes: Target-size audit guidance: separate the 44 px aspiration from the 24 px requirement; an actionable finding names page, viewport, target, clickable dimensions, nearby controls, exception analysis, and user consequence; remediation enlarges the hit area, increases spacing, or changes the shared component; retest after the change ships, including responsive states.

sources.title: Interop 2026 announcement: focus areas
sources.notes: 2026 cross-browser focus areas relevant to interface patterns: anchor positioning, scroll-driven animations, view transitions (incl. cross-document), dialog/popover additions (closedby, popover=hint), container style queries, contrast-color().

sources.title: Loading states and skeleton screens in Figma
sources.notes: Skeleton loading rules: 1-10s window for skeletons, match final layout box for box, replace each placeholder as content arrives, never show empty state during fetch, aria-busy/aria-live announcements, static reduced-motion variant, readable skeleton contrast.

sources.title: Television interface design tips
sources.notes: Type minimums on TV (~12sp minimum, 18sp default; ~24pt practical floor at 3m), light text on dark backgrounds, short scannable copy, safe margins, remote input planning per variant.

sources.title: TV style guidelines (platform documentation)
sources.notes: 10-foot UI style rules: focus visibility, type scale, colour and contrast handling on television panels.

sources.title: TV layout guidelines (platform documentation)
sources.notes: Television layout composition: shelves, hero rows, section bars, playback screens and input handling.

sources.title: Television interface best practices
sources.notes: Best practices: focus memory, text-entry avoidance, second-device handoff for complex flows, performance on constrained hardware.

sources.title: Designing a 10-foot interface
sources.notes: 10-foot UI rules: viewing distance variance, type legibility at distance, focus indicators, safe areas.

sources.title: Rethinking interface design for the TV platform
sources.notes: TV platform design: overscan-safe margins (~5%), centre-weighted gaze, near-white (#f1f1f1) to reduce flicker, avoid pure white and over-saturated reds.

sources.title: Window size classes
sources.notes: Standardised width bands: compact <600dp, medium 600-840dp, expanded 840-1200dp; layout changes follow bands, not device names.

sources.title: Two-pane layout guidance
sources.notes: List-detail two-pane threshold at ~600dp width; supporting-pane splits (~70/30 expanded, ~50/50 medium, stacked or bottom-sheet at compact).

sources.title: Foldable states and postures
sources.notes: Foldable postures: flat behaves like a tablet; tabletop posture splits viewing and controls; book posture keeps content clear of the crease; never place interactive elements across the fold; preserve in-progress state across fold changes.

sources.title: Canonical layouts overview
sources.notes: Canonical adaptive layouts: list-detail, feed, supporting pane; navigation switches with width class (bottom nav, rail, permanent drawer).

sources.title: Designing for tiny wearable screens
sources.notes: Wearable constraints: 2-5 second task window, one primary item per screen, multi-tap tasks move to the phone app, haptic confirmation.

sources.title: Designing for a small smartwatch screen
sources.notes: Small-screen rules: 38-48dp targets spaced 8pt apart, full-screen swipe navigation, rotating crown as primary scroll mechanism.

sources.title: Wearable app information architecture principles
sources.notes: Wearable IA: glanceable tiles are non-scrollable, ambient/always-on simplified state, dark interfaces for battery, minimal background work.

sources.title: Tiles (wearable design documentation)
sources.notes: Glanceable information surfaces: non-scrollable tiles, single glance reading, tap leads to detail on another surface.

sources.title: Apps (wearable design documentation)
sources.notes: Wearable app structure: long-press for context menus, edge gestures, round-display margins (round offers ~22% less usable space than square).

sources.title: Design for wearables (platform documentation)
sources.notes: Wearable design entry: glanceability as structural constraint, input modalities, ambient vs active states.

sources.title: E-paper display vs LCD comparison
sources.notes: E-paper is reflective and bistable: image persists with zero power, energy only during refreshes; sunlight-readable, no glow in the dark.

sources.title: E-paper vs e-ink differences
sources.notes: E-paper characteristics: update intervals of minutes to hours are normal; unsuitable for video, smooth animation, rapid scrolling (~1Hz typical refresh).

sources.title: E-paper ghosting explained
sources.notes: Ghosting from repeated partial updates; periodic full refreshes clear residue; redraw only changed regions between full refreshes.

sources.title: E-paper display optimisation notes
sources.notes: E-paper optimisation: fixed-height static layouts, high-contrast black-on-white styling, debounced inputs against input lag.

sources.title: E-paper display management (refresh logic)
sources.notes: Refresh scheduling for e-paper: partial updates for changed regions, scheduled full refreshes that briefly flash the display.

sources.title: Hero section patterns and conversion examples
sources.notes: Outcome-first heroes: named audience, measurable outcome headline, one primary action, proof point before first scroll, product shown in motion.

sources.title: Landing page conversion tips and form friction benchmarks
sources.notes: Form friction: three-field lead forms vs nine-field drop-off; multi-step forms beat a single wall of fields; section order mirrors the decision.

sources.title: Hero layout patterns and when-to-use table
sources.notes: Hero variants: left-text/right-visual, centred text over image, embedded form in hero; social proof placed where doubt appears, adjacent to actions.

sources.title: Passwordless design: autofill passkey sign-in
sources.notes: Highest-converting passkey UX puts passkeys in the username autofill dropdown via conditional mediation; no standalone sign-in-with-passkey button.

sources.title: Passkey UX patterns: fallback chain, QR handoff, enrollment
sources.notes: Fallback chain (passkey, app push, email magic link, email OTP, SMS last); visible fallbacks; one-time enrollment prompt; QR cross-device handoff needs context first; credential management page with rename and revoke.

sources.title: Settings page UI guide: layout types and edit patterns
sources.notes: Sidebar/list navigation beats icon grids; edit chrome follows stakes: inline for low-stakes, modal where focus is warranted, confirmation for destructive actions.

sources.title: Settings search design and zero-result logging
sources.notes: Settings search heuristic: 20+ fields warrants search; match user synonyms; results state section and current value; zero-result searches logged as research.

sources.title: Dangerous actions: danger zone pattern
sources.notes: Danger zone: grouped irreversible actions at the bottom, visually distinct; state the effect before commit; require extra effort (re-entry, type-to-confirm) since page access is not proof of identity.

sources.title: Comparison tables as decision machines
sources.notes: Differences-only toggle hiding identical rows; gentle winner marking with shading plus text cue (never colour alone); computed deltas; explicit metric direction.

sources.title: Pricing page optimisation: cards vs matrix
sources.notes: Tier-card discipline: 3-4 columns, plain audience labels, 'everything in the previous tier plus' summaries, sticky plan labels and decision row, annual saving spelled out.

sources.title: Mobile permission timing and two-stage flow
sources.notes: Two-stage permission flow: custom pre-permission screen stating concrete value, system dialog only after positive response; never ask on first launch; one permission at a time; graceful denial with route to settings.

sources.title: Search UI design: no-results recovery
sources.notes: Ordered no-results recovery: spelling suggestion, broaden scope, removable carried filters, create action; echo the exact query+filter combination; never silently clear.

sources.title: SaaS empty search: keep filters visible
sources.notes: Keep query and filters visible on empty results; echo what matched nothing; label each widening action by what it changes.

sources.title: Website search design best practices 2026
sources.notes: Search/filter handoff: search narrows by intent, filters by attribute; mirrored chips; single reset clears filters but keeps query; facet panels with live result counts.

sources.title: Headless component libraries compared
sources.notes: 2026 norm is headless behaviour-only primitives: focus management, keyboard maps, roles and states, portals, collision-aware positioning, unstyled elements with data-state attributes; behaviour is the durable half.

sources.title: Enterprise component suite 2026 volume 3 release
sources.notes: Enterprise release: drag-and-drop form builder with 20+ built-in form components; date-field rebuild with per-part keyboard entry and opt-in confirmation for the calendar popover.

sources.title: Design system update notes, February-March 2026
sources.notes: Design-system update: date-field accessibility rebuild, callout promotion, new tokens (sub-size icons, highlight backgrounds, raised-surface elevation).

sources.title: Data-table changelog 2026
sources.notes: Data-table refinements: cell-level actions, grouped loading per section, expanded rows aligned to the visible viewport, sticky-header and fixed-column alignment fixes.

sources.title: Barge-in benchmark write-up
sources.notes: Interruption budget: users forgive ~600ms to answer but not ~600ms of continued speech after being cut off; +120ms on the interruption path reads as rudeness; target 200-300ms stop pipeline.

sources.title: Full-duplex voice architecture
sources.notes: Stop-mid-sentence pipeline: detect user speech, stop audio, cancel in-progress generation, re-enter listening; learned turn-taking lands end-of-turn around 200-250ms.

sources.title: Voice user interfaces in 2026
sources.notes: 2026 voice interfaces fuse speech with visual context, gestures and camera input; confirmations via haptic pulses and spatial audio; voice layered into real workflows with visual context.

sources.title: Conversational design guide 2026
sources.notes: Turn-taking rhythm: chunked responses, intentional pauses; error recovery by rephrase, tappable options, or handoff; spoken fallbacks in voice-only contexts, never buttons alone.

sources.title: Spatial computing lesson: field of view and depth zones
sources.notes: Comfort zones: primary zone ~40-degree cone around centre gaze, secondary 20-40 degrees off-axis; placement height 1.2-1.5m; arm's length for detailed work, 1-3m for viewing, beyond 3m ambient only.

sources.title: VR interface design guide
sources.notes: VR layout ergonomics: flat panels for precision data and forms, curved panels for panoramic dashboards with radius matched to focal distance (2-3m); never force upward neck tilt beyond ~15 degrees.

sources.title: Adding XR to existing apps
sources.notes: 2D apps run as 2D panels inside 3D space; spatial dialogs fall back to standard 2D dialogs; capability tiers per component with documented fallbacks.

sources.title: Multi-window spatial layout SDK
sources.notes: Multi-window spatial systems cap promoted panels with per-window fallback modes (inline vs drop) and priority ordering when slots run out.

sources.title: Interface trends 2026: spatial glass interfaces
sources.notes: Translucent multi-layer panels are the 2026 spatial look; legibility testing to WCAG AA minimum on translucent backgrounds; user toggle to high-contrast opaque; blur costs frame rate and battery.

sources.title: From UX to task-doing experience: six trust patterns
sources.notes: Six trust patterns across the action lifecycle: intent preview, autonomy dial, explainable rationale, confidence signal, action audit and undo, escalation pathway.

sources.title: Interface design for automated assistants
sources.notes: Orchestration surface: editable plan steps, tool-use disclosure at the decision moment, visible memory corrections; post-action receipts summarising changes, systems touched, assumptions, and what can still be undone.

sources.title: Intent-based experience: orchestration surface
sources.notes: Intent UX: full orchestration surface for multi-step high-stakes tasks, lighter disclosure for low-stakes single steps; plan visibility and approval granularity.

sources.title: CSS-only scroll-driven animations
sources.notes: Scroll timeline API is cross-browser: animations tied to scroll position without scripts; reduced-motion handling: swap movement for calm, ship a deliberate final static state per effect.

sources.title: Scroll-driven CSS carousels in 2026
sources.notes: Full carousels in pure CSS (scroll-snap, scroll markers, view timelines) with @supports fallbacks to plain scroll containers; accessibility guards.

sources.title: Website animation guidance: layout-shift costs
sources.notes: Animate only transform and opacity (GPU-accelerated); never width/height; layout-shifting animations feed cumulative layout shift; reduced-motion safety net keeps essential feedback.

sources.title: Web design principles 2026
sources.notes: Scroll-driven motion replacing parallax; visible pause-animation controls; keep the fade, drop the travel; small contained motion retained.

sources.notes: Platform UI kit: popups default to the anchor's width; new checkbox, radio group, and switch controls.

sources.notes: Accessibility-first direction: keyboard focus must not be hidden by author-created content; dragging needs a simple pointer alternative; 24 px pointer target minimum.

sources.notes: Four responsive table strategies: horizontal scroll with frozen column, card transformation, column dropping by priority, priority-plus disclosure; selection rule is which columns a person cannot decide without

sources.notes: Sticky positioning preferred over fixed for frozen columns; corner-cell overlap ordering; stacked card layout via data-label attributes for compact screens

sources.notes: Goal setting for contextual onboarding paths; one-click setup, progress indicators, skip where not necessary, smart defaults; guided first action toward the aha moment

sources.title: Onboarding UX best strategies for seamless journeys
sources.notes: Progressive disclosure of signup steps; value before account; lead with a success action; default content or templates to reach value fast

sources.title: Why most in-app onboarding fails (and how to fix it in 2026)
sources.notes: Mechanism-agnostic onboarding: checklist, contextual guidance, prefilled workspace; items must map to outcome events, not a feature tour; one signup question routes what follows

sources.title: Drag-and-drop menus in 2026: mouse, touch, and accessibility
sources.notes: Drag as progressive enhancement over a keyboard-usable menu; unified pointer handling; semantic navigation; reorder alternatives that do not require dragging

sources.title: Keyboard navigation patterns every developer should know
sources.notes: Menu keyboard models: tab to each item for flat nav, arrow-key navigation inside menubar composites; roving tab index; escape returns focus to the trigger

sources.title: Component library changelog: theme resolution and accessible-label translations
sources.notes: October 2026: automatic color mode follows the live system preference on every reload; configured theme preset authoritative over stale cookie; aria.* translation namespace for accessible labels across components.

sources.title: Developer's guide to interface internationalization (2026)
sources.notes: Locale-specific formatting for dates, numbers, currency, time; right-to-left layout mirroring via logical CSS properties and the dir attribute; runtime language switching without restart.

sources.title: Bidirectionality usability guidance
sources.notes: RTL mirroring rules: layouts flip, directional icons mirror, text keeps its own language direction; not mirrored: numbers, charts and graphs, non-directional icons, media playback controls and progress direction.

sources.title: UI card design: grid layouts, spacing and density (2026)
sources.notes: Card grid density by breakpoint: fewer columns when each choice is a decision, more for browsing; 12-16px minimum gutter floor; density trades breathing room for comparability; infinite scroll vs pagination vs load-more for long grids.

sources.title: Realizing common layouts using CSS grid
sources.notes: Flexible card grids via repeat(auto-fit, minmax()); spanning tiles backfill gaps with grid-auto-flow: dense only when items have no set order, since display order then diverges from source and tab order.

sources.title: Accessible data visualizations
sources.notes: Charts highlight trends and outliers while tables carry precise values; descriptive takeaway titles, text alternatives with key insights, colour never alone, keyboard and screen-reader compatible, underlying data offered as a table.

sources.title: Command-palette usability guidance
sources.notes: Stable selection while results update; no broad fuzzy match above the intended costly action; show scope with the name.

sources.title: SaaS command-palette and search UX patterns
sources.notes: Command-palette pattern: autofocus, subsequence matching, grouped typed results, recents in the empty state; typeahead per-row context; search-health metrics.

sources.title: Command-palette UI design guide and teardowns
sources.notes: Palette as teaching surface for shortcuts; frecency-ranked recents; grouping by result type.

sources.title: Notification UX: urgency-to-pattern mapping
sources.notes: Urgency scale mapped to pattern and channel; notification debt from high-urgency patterns on low-urgency events.

sources.title: SaaS notification and toast UX patterns
sources.notes: Nothing critical only in a toast; disruption level decides inline alert vs toast vs banner vs modal.

sources.title: Offline-first frontend apps: local store and background sync
sources.notes: Local store as source of truth; durable mutation queue with identifiers and attempt counts; background-sync replay with fallbacks.

sources.title: Frontend system design: offline support and progressive web apps
sources.notes: Granular sync states: syncing, local changes pending, stale; optimistic updates marked pending; visible sync status with retry.

sources.title: Upload UI components: chunking and resumable uploads
sources.notes: Per-file queue items with progress and retry; chunked resumable uploads; accurate progress after interruption.

sources.title: Automotive HMI design: glance budgets and essential functions
sources.notes: Two-second glance and twelve-second task budgets; physical controls for essential functions; voice for secondary tasks.

sources.title: HMI design principles for automotive interfaces
sources.notes: Contextual minimalism and progressive disclosure by driving conditions; adaptive interfaces over show-everything.

sources.title: Web Awesome vs Shoelace: web-component library succession
sources.notes: Successor web-components library: component count, colour palettes, cascade layers, SSR support, commercial additions.

sources.title: Component library direction 2026: unstyled primitives and data components
sources.notes: Stable unstyled-primitives layer with token theming; number-field control; data-line grid-chart integration and server-side pivoting.

sources.title: Reduced-motion fixes: informational versus decorative animation
sources.notes: Informational motion keeps moving; decorative motion gated behind a no-preference check so it fails closed to static.

sources.title: Focus indicators: contrast, forced colours, and obscured focus
sources.notes: 3:1 non-text contrast for focus indicators; outline in system colours for forced-colours mode; focus not obscured by fixed chrome.

sources.title: Glass-mode theming handbook
sources.notes: Never layer glass containers; glass disables under high-contrast mode; default opacities treated as accessibility-tested values.

sources.title: Introducing the Accessible Components Library
sources.notes: v1.0.0 release of an accessibility-documented component set (accordion, breadcrumbs, dialog, disclosure, pagination, tabs, text input, textarea); per-component WCAG 2.2 success-criteria mapping, test scenarios, assistive-technology compatibility notes, and usability recommendations beyond the standard.

sources.title: Beyond border-radius: what the CSS corner-shape property unlocks for everyday UI
sources.notes: Native CSS geometric shape control: corner-shape presets (bevel, notch, scoop, squircle) available in Chromium, border-shape and shape() function in the borders/shapes specifications; practical guidance for progressive enhancement with rectangular fallbacks.

sources.title: Driving-task interface design principles
sources.notes: Two-second glance budget with 0.25 s input response; one-handed gestures; 76x76 dp targets with 23 dp spacing; 32/24 dp text; day/night modes; distraction suppression while moving; interruption and resumption of non-driving tasks.

sources.title: Automotive glance budgets and interaction economics
sources.notes: Glance budget of about 2 s per glance and 12 s per task; design for glances not taps with one question answered per glance; stable information positions; physical controls required for essential functions; shallow fast touch flows can outperform button-heavy ones.

sources.title: Self-service kiosk UX checklist
sources.notes: One task per screen with always-visible back, home, and cancel controls; 9-12 mm touch targets; error recovery without staff help; timeout warnings with countdown and one-tap session reset; 15-48 inch control reach; offline fallback; multilingual entry points.

sources.title: Accessibility requirements for self-service terminals
sources.notes: The accessibility entry point must itself be usable without vision; multi-sense time-limit alerts with extension; 800-1600 mm placement bounds; printed information also available through speech; speech output, tactile keys, and headset support need hands-on testing with speech-output users.

sources.title: Map interaction patterns
sources.notes: MapTip hover notes; visited markers mirroring visited links; small multiples for comparing change over time; peel-back swipe to reveal the layer underneath; info pop-up for short detail versus info panel for long or interactive content; rich markers with a key metric.

sources.title: Chat and messaging interface patterns
sources.notes: Element set: multi-line input, visible send, distinguished bubbles, grouped timestamps, typing and read indicators; errors belong on the failed message bubble with inline resend; offline messages queue and send on reconnect; capabilities stated up front; quick actions and suggested prompts; streamed responses with a stop option; live-region announcements.

sources.title: Infinite scroll versus pagination
sources.notes: Infinite scroll for exploratory browsing, pagination for goal-oriented tasks; pagination gives structure, sense of place, and reliable back-button behaviour; load-more button as the safe default; infinite scroll needs loading indicators, place-restoring URL updates, back-to-top, live-region announcements, and a paginated fallback for crawlers.

sources.title: Multi-step process design: wizards and stepped flows
sources.notes: Total step count shown up front; completed/current/future steps distinctly marked with future steps visible but non-interactive; short specific step labels; vertical stepper on narrow screens; contextual forward labels; data-preserving back; save-and-resume for flows longer than a few minutes.

sources.title: Dashboard design principles
sources.notes: Three-slot key-figure tiles (number, delta with direction, comparison window); colour encodes meaning only with grayscale readability; roughly 3:1 density ratio between primary and secondary zones; always-visible removable filter chips; update cadence matched to the decision cycle with a stated last-updated time.

sources.title: Date picker design: anatomy to accessibility
sources.notes: Lightest control for the intent: typed field, picker, or full calendar; ranges as their own pattern with two-month view and hover preview; seven mutually-distinguishable day-cell states; typed entry as a first-class path; full keyboard contract with focus management and announced day cells.

sources.title: Date and time picker patterns for reporting and scheduling tools
sources.notes: Each intent gets its own control (single date, date-and-time with timezone, linked range, relative/recurring); time values state timezone unambiguously; presets put common intents one tap away; unavailable dates are unpickable and explained in place; ranges commit explicitly.

sources.title: APCA: the perceptual contrast algorithm
sources.notes: Lightness-contrast score roughly 0-120 replacing fixed ratios; polarity-aware with size and weight factored in; proposed thresholds near 90 body, 75 large/bold, 60 floor, 45 non-text; practical stance: keep the 2.x AA baseline and test new palettes against both systems.

sources.title: Dark mode design rules
sources.notes: Dark greys not pure black, off-white not pure white; typography adjustments (weight, size, line height, spacing); elevation by lighter surface tones instead of shadows; redesigned accents; semantic token contract across themes; system preference default with user override; 200-300 ms switch honouring reduced motion; test on OLED, LCD, and e-ink.

sources.title: UI/UX Design Trends 2026: 10 Verdicts for Product Teams
sources.notes: Translucent materials acceptable on navigation and controls, risky on text/number-dense content screens: contrast shifts as content scrolls beneath; keep translucency out of the content layer and honour reduce-transparency and increase-contrast settings.

sources.title: Inside a Design System That Teaches Automated Tooling What It Is Not Allowed to Change
sources.notes: Components carry machine-readable metadata marking required safety controls versus removable convenience; automated assembly may rearrange and restyle but cannot delete a protected check. Accessibility rules written in machine-readable form travel with the component.

sources.title: Design Systems in October 2026: Built for Machines. Still Governed by Humans.
sources.notes: Empty-state evolution: interfaces pre-populating from available context before the user acts, replacing a static blank empty screen; suggestions must stay visually distinct from real items and remain dismissible, never stored as user data.

sources.title: 12 UI/UX Design Trends for AI Apps (2026 + Examples)
sources.notes: Ambient adaptation with visible, reversible, explainable change indicators; confidence indicators for outputs where factual accuracy matters — corroborates pre-populated suggestion states that disclose their nature.

sources.title: The Empty State Is Your Best Growth Surface and Nobody Designs It
sources.notes: Worked-example empty states: a pre-filled sample marked as an example with an adopt action; faded preview of the populated state where sampling is impossible.

sources.title: UX for AI Agents: Designing Interfaces That Machines Use
sources.notes: Machine-facing UX: structured content, API-first design, machine-readable docs, predictable error schemas, performance.

sources.title: Agent-First Design Paradigms: Adapting UX for AI as a New User
sources.notes: Agent-first patterns: semantic markup, agent-mode shadow views, verification checkpoints for high-risk actions.

sources.title: Agent Experience First Design (AXFD): Designing Systems for a Non-Human User
sources.notes: AXFD principles: contract-first APIs, typed failures with retryable hints and partial results, idempotent re-entrant operations, checkpoints, observability.

sources.title: Machine Experience (MX): Designing For AI Agents In 2026
sources.notes: Agentic UX by intent: informational (extractable facts), navigational (site maps), commercial (comparison tables), transactional (agent-ready forms).

sources.title: Agentic UX: Designing Interfaces for AI Agents, Not Humans
sources.notes: Invisible UX: schemas and APIs as the interface, label consistency as usability, agent-decision traceability.

sources.title: Design Systems for AI Agents
sources.notes: Agent-ready design systems: machine-readable tokens, documented component APIs, design-to-code parity.

sources.title: Building Bulletproof RTL Design Systems
sources.notes: Bidirectional design systems: mirror-vs-not-mirror checklist, logical properties, component-by-component RTL breakdown.

sources.title: RTL Is Not a Mirror Toggle: A Practical Checklist for Multilingual Web Tools
sources.notes: RTL checklist: logical CSS properties, mirror navigation not meaning, progress and carousel direction behavior.

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System: what's new (Frontend v6.6.0, October 2026)
sources.notes: Frontend v6.6.0 refines the character count component; new component lifecycle statuses: new components (Feedback, Language navigation) release as 'Trial' while usage guidance is gathered.

sources.title: UI Trends 2026 vs 2027: What Stays, What Goes, What to Fix
sources.notes: Late-October 2026 trend survey: the interface that assembles itself at runtime is the year's biggest shift; design intent must be written down explicitly where the assembler can read it, otherwise the result is the median default. Also covers platform visual-language sliders and the fading of unchosen defaults.

sources.title: Tiled payment-method checkout layout
sources.notes: Payment-method selection moves from a vertical list to a tiled grid for four or fewer methods, applied automatically at platform level starting late October 2026; five or more methods keep the list view. Tiles make methods easier to scan at a glance ahead of peak-season traffic.

sources.title: Interface design direction 2026-2027: beyond new morphisms
sources.notes: Design-direction review: simulated materials (soft, metallic, transparent, reflective) should support meaning rather than decorate; depth should communicate hierarchy with restraint instead of floating everything; motion should explain relationships between states while staying accessible; surface treatment should adapt to product context rather than apply as a universal filter.

sources.title: WCAG 3.0 September 2026 draft: one conformance level, six tiers
sources.notes: September 2026 WCAG 3.0 working draft replaces A/AA/AAA with one conformance level (all core requirements) plus six reporting tiers (Avoid physical harm, Foundational access, Conformance, Bronze, Silver, Gold) and four impact tags (physical harm, risk, barrier, friction); still a draft, 2.2 AA remains the practical target.

sources.title: Spatial computing UI/UX ergonomics for visionOS in 2026
sources.notes: VisionOS spatial design ergonomics: eyes as targeting cursor with gaze-hover intent confirmation before gestures, lap-level thumb-index pinch as primary input, positional audio anchors for feedback and attention redirection, no stacked translucent panels, 60x60 pt minimum targets.

sources.title: SaaS form design without friction
sources.notes: Form collection framework: ask, infer, defer, or confirm per field; smart defaults only for low-risk choices; unknown-outcome recovery treats timeouts as unknown rather than failed, verifying before retry so duplicates cannot be created.

sources.title: Agent checkpoints, memory, provenance, and spatial widgets
sources.notes: Emerging pattern set: visible checkpoints in multi-step automated flows (delegate, monitor, approve, interrupt, refine), memory as an inspectable and resettable primitive, provenance answers at a glance on synthetic or third-party media.

sources.title: Bottom-sheet mobile menus in thumb reach
sources.notes: Mobile menus opening from the bottom edge place every item in the one-handed thumb zone; a 2026 survey cited bottom sheets in 71% of top-100 mobile apps for primary navigation, up from 28% in 2022. Statistic from search summary; verify before citing numerically.

sources.title: Replacing onboarding tours with contextual help
sources.notes: Three-level help ladder: passive help passing a five-second test, gentle nudges on first meaningful interaction, rescue help only after repeated friction; replaces blocking tours with escalating guidance. From search summary; verify before quoting the five-second test wording.

sources.title: Container-query responsiveness in 2026 frontend trends
sources.notes: Components should adapt to their container size rather than only the viewport: the same component must reflow correctly in a full page, sidebar, modal, or dense dashboard grid.

sources.title: Voice interaction patterns for hybrid voice and touch flows
sources.notes: Voice mishearing repair as a visual safety net: show what was heard and offer tappable correction instead of a dead-end 'not understood' message.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 checklist for machine-generated interfaces
sources.notes: Release-day accessibility pass for agent-rendered UI: automated scan first, keyboard-only manual pass second; WCAG 2.2 checks (focus not obscured, dragging alternatives, 24 px targets, consistent help, redundant entry, accessible authentication); residual-risk recording; re-run on every regeneration.

sources.title: Designing human-in-the-loop checkpoints for agent interfaces
sources.notes: Checkpoint design for agent products: gate before the run for standing tool access, gate after the draft for one-off actions with a clear preview; approval cards must show the payload (recipient, diff, amount, tool); pair checkpoints with autonomy budgets; skip checkpoints on low-stakes reversible actions.

sources.title: Agentic design patterns: human-in-the-loop controls
sources.notes: Human-in-the-loop as a deliberate design choice: checkpoints pause execution, surface reasoning and the proposed action, and wait for confirmation; checkpoint tiers (pre-production gate, ambiguous findings, security-sensitive scope); risk-based escalation for where review belongs.

sources.title: Multimodal input area and feedback design
sources.notes: Multimodal input area: text box, mic button, and camera/upload entry with a mode hint; waveform while listening, thumbnails for attachments, processing states; the system echoes what it understood so mishearing is correctable; vision results show what was detected with correction options.

sources.title: Voice agent interaction patterns: surface modes and input mechanisms
sources.notes: Voice agent perceived role: full-screen voice mode versus inline voice inside the thread; push-to-talk versus voice-activity-detection trade-offs; complex output such as code, tables, and artefacts cannot be spoken and must route back to the text surface.

sources.title: UX design trends 2026-2027: act-now table
sources.notes: 2026-2027 trend table with act-now versus can-wait guidance: agentic UX, generative and adaptive UI, multimodal interfaces, transparency patterns, accessibility baseline, privacy-aware personalization; the through-line is design work shifting toward trust, control, and clarity.

sources.title: UI/UX design trends 2026: calm, adaptive, token-based
sources.notes: 2026 trend guide: adaptive interfaces, accessibility as infrastructure, calm design, purposeful motion, token-based design systems; interfaces that respect user attention rather than compete for it.

sources.title: Kinetic typography without overwhelming users
sources.notes: Kinetic type guidance: motion as punctuation not prose, static-first design with reduced-motion fallback, whole-word screen-reader announcements, compositor-friendly properties, user control over looping motion; published 2026-10-01.

sources.title: Human-in-the-loop approval for agent systems
sources.notes: Approval pattern: one enforcement point for consequential actions, per-action decisions (cleared, approval-required, denied), a named approver, and a receipt recorded before the action runs; a changed amount or recipient needs a new decision.

sources.title: Human-in-the-loop placements in agent execution
sources.notes: Four placements: approval gates for irreversible actions, escalation on low confidence or failure, steering pauses for guidance, and outcome review before release; interruptibility requires persistent checkpoints so a paused run resumes from saved state.

sources.title: Human-in-the-loop approval workflows
sources.notes: Control loop: agent proposes an action, pauses, routes to a human approver, and resumes only on approval; approve, edit, and reject decision types with per-action review configuration.

sources.title: Voice interface design principles
sources.notes: Voice principles: design for natural phrasing, keep responses short with the key point first, confirm what was heard (implicit for low stakes, explicit for high stakes), and treat misrecognition recovery as a first-class flow with narrower choices rather than a repeated apology.

sources.title: Using container size and style queries
sources.notes: Container queries: declare a containment context with container-type (size or inline-size), query the nearest container with @container, size features include width, height, inline-size, block-size, aspect-ratio, and orientation; containment is required to avoid layout loops.

sources.title: Watch platform widget and live-activity update
sources.notes: Watch platform shift from full-screen cards to composable small tiles (2x1 or 2x2) for glanceable data, plus a persistent live-activity tracker anchored at the bottom of the watch face and the top of the notification tray.

sources.title: Multimodal input user experience guidance
sources.notes: Voice entry lands as editable text before sending; media attachments appear as removable thumbnails; switching input modes keeps the composed message.

sources.title: Offline-first form conflict resolution
sources.notes: Send only changed fields with an expected version; auto-merge fields changed on one side only, ask the person when both sides changed the same field; keep saved-local and synced as separate states.

sources.title: Voice interface design best practices including command discoverability
sources.notes: Commands are invisible, so discovery needs contextual suggestions, examples inside replies, and progressive introduction of advanced commands rather than a single tour.

sources.title: Smartwatch interface design: glanceable surfaces and staged disclosure
sources.notes: Glanceable watch surfaces: one datum and one action per screen, dark always-on variants for battery, and sensitive notifications shown as a generic alert first with detail revealed only after a deliberate gesture.

sources.title: Pointer-based television navigation alongside directional navigation
sources.notes: Pointer and directional navigation operate in parallel on television surfaces: the pointer targets any visible element directly while directional movement follows a fixed focus order, so the interface must keep one stable logical focus and make scroll containers and overlays work under both input modes.

sources.title: Notification fatigue: batching and digest strategies for product notifications
sources.notes: Consolidate low-urgency updates into periodic digests (time-based, threshold-based, or engagement-timed) so one summary replaces many interruptions; group related events for context and let the person control types, channels, and frequency.

sources.title: The ethics of personalization: transparency, control, and diversity in adapted content
sources.notes: Responsible adaptation explains why content appears, offers opt-outs and resets, keeps diverse content in view, and gives people real choices over what is adapted rather than silent adaptation.

sources.title: Settings page design: organising preferences and making changes clear
sources.notes: Separate account-wide preferences from device, workspace, or project settings; group related choices under plain headings, keep destructive actions distinct, state save behaviour explicitly, and show pending, saved, and failed states with recovery.

sources.title: Designing user-centred scheduling interfaces: availability, time zones, and quick interactions
sources.notes: Scheduling surfaces make availability unmistakable (available, pending, booked), mark time zones, holidays, and non-working hours, offer filters by person, location, or service, and keep tap targets and quick actions usable on small screens.

sources.title: Cancellation flow research: transparent versus obstructive exit paths
sources.notes: Cancellation stays in the sign-up channel with a plain label, states what ends and when before confirmation, offers pause or plan change beside cancellation rather than as a gate, and confirms the end date and resume path in writing.

sources.title: Cross-device task handoff: resume a task on another device
sources.notes: A task started on one device appears as a resume suggestion on a nearby signed-in second device, reopening the same screen and state; where the app is absent, the task opens in a browser view instead.

sources.title: Keyboard shortcut guidance: standard shortcuts, mnemonic assignments, and single-character shortcut controls
sources.notes: Shortcuts follow standard assignments where they exist, use mnemonic combinations for new actions, stay reachable with one hand for common operations, and single-character shortcuts are controllable so spoken input does not trigger actions by accident.

sources.title: Biometric authentication sign-in guidance: opt-in timing, prompt ownership, fallback, and failure handling
sources.notes: Offer biometric sign-in after a first successful sign-in rather than during registration, always include a password or PIN fallback, the operating system owns the prompt while the app designs timing and framing, show the option only where the device supports it, and treat cancellation as a return rather than an error.

sources.title: Voice turn-taking and recovery guidance
sources.notes: Resume from the last confirmed-played boundary after a false interruption; a genuine correction stops playback, cancels pending writes, and is preserved; after a dropped connection treat playback as unknown unless a receipt proves it; reconcile receipts before retrying so a reconnected request never takes effect twice.

sources.title: Data Table Design: 9 Best Practices (2026 Guide)
sources.notes: Use a table to scan and compare many records; for large sets add sorting, filtering, and search, paginate or lazy-load rows, freeze the header, use sticky headers with virtualised or paginated rows, let people control density and visible columns, and never load everything at once.

sources.title: Accessible form validation and error recovery pattern
sources.notes: Validate on submit or save rather than while typing; summarise several errors in a list near the top with focus moved to it, focus the single invalid field when there is only one error, always show failing fields as invalid with messages, and retain entered input after a failed submission.

sources.title: Mobile Onboarding UX: Reduce Drop-Off and Boost Activation
sources.notes: Use inline help as the default, tooltips for genuinely ambiguous elements, and coach marks sparingly: show them when the person first reaches the relevant feature, always allow dismissal, and never chain more than three in sequence.

sources.title: The UX of Empty States: Designing Moments of Nothing
sources.notes: An empty state must explain the absence and offer a next action rather than ending the journey; build it as a static fallback that renders even when the data request fails, and translate raw error codes into plain language with a next step.

sources.title: UX for reversible actions: A decision framework for designing with recovery in mind
sources.notes: Match the recovery pattern to impact and frequency: undo for low-impact frequent actions, trash for moderate occasional deletions, version history for high-impact collaborative work; make recovery options visible, consistent, and time-bound, and state the recovery window plainly.

sources.title: Time Zone Scheduling UX: Local Times, DST, and Recurring Events
sources.notes: Pin recurring events to a named zone rather than a fixed offset so clock changes never silently shift them; preview how each attendee's local time changes across a transition before confirming; flag ambiguous or repeated times around zone transitions; a temporary hold needs an explicit deadline and an availability check after expiry.

sources.title: Use split screen on your Pixel Tablet
sources.notes: Two apps side by side on a tablet: drag the divider to resize, double-tap it to swap positions, drag text or images between compatible apps, save an app pair for one-tap reopening, and drag the divider fully to one side to close one app.

sources.title: Progressive web apps complete guide
sources.notes: Install-prompt timing and behaviour: offer installation after engagement rather than on first visit, keep a dismissal dismissed, state the benefit beside the action, and give manual install steps where the platform offers no prompt event.

sources.title: Branching conversation documentation
sources.notes: Branching from any message: the new branch inherits the conversation up to that message, the original thread stays unchanged and reachable, branches are labelled by intent, and earlier answers stay reviewable instead of being overwritten.

sources.title: Keyboard navigation and chart explorer for embedded visualisations
sources.notes: Point-by-point chart explorer entered from the plot area: arrow keys move between data points, legend selection, zoom and search stay keyboard-reachable, the focused region stays visible when zoomed, and movement geometry follows chart type — free for scatter plots and maps, along one axis and within series for line, area and stacked charts, along the horizontal axis only for waterfall, small-multiple and grouped-column charts.

sources.title: Paywall trial-offer guidance
sources.notes: Paywall trial offers must state explicitly whether a trial is included; a control that adds or removes a trial must not double as the purchase confirmation, so changing the trial cannot silently commit the person to an auto-renewing charge.

sources.title: Avoid data loss and timeouts: session timeout design pattern
sources.notes: Avoid timeouts and let the person save work as they go; where a timeout is unavoidable, state the time available and whether entered data will be lost when starting the process, and offer a simple extension without data loss.

sources.title: Session timeout warning guidance
sources.notes: A session timeout warning stays visible, never blocks continued work, shows time remaining where known, and offers extension or sign-out; after expiry the person is told the session ended and offered a way back in.

sources.title: Import and export transfer patterns: partial results and progress
sources.notes: A transfer shows real progress, distinguishes receiving from processing, states whether leaving cancels the operation, and reports partial results by added, updated, skipped, and failed counts rather than calling the whole operation a success or a failure.

sources.title: Account deletion with a grace period: what is removed and what is kept
sources.notes: Account deletion runs in the same channel as sign-up, signs the person out everywhere at once, states a dated grace period with a plain keep-account path, lists what is removed and what is kept with retention periods, and confirms completion in writing.

sources.title: The perfect file upload pattern
sources.notes: File upload guidance: where a suitable file is already held, offer it as a one-step reuse choice before asking for a fresh upload; the upload itself is the most labour-intensive form interaction, so avoiding it where possible is the strongest improvement.

sources.title: Designing tables with lots of data
sources.notes: Data table guidance: columns ordered by importance, sticky header and first column, explicit sort state, active filters with one-click clear, columns that can be hidden and reordered without relying on drag alone, adjustable density, truncation with the full value available, and editing in a side panel that keeps compared rows in view.

sources.title: How to Build Offline-Tolerant Web Apps That Recover Cleanly
sources.notes: Offline-tolerant sync guidance: distinguish saved locally from synchronised remotely with a small status vocabulary; derive operational status from queue progress and real request outcomes rather than a connectivity signal alone; use persistent badges near affected records and a central sync panel instead of a toast per transition; keep optimistic display to reversible edits and keep consequential actions unconfirmed until the server confirms them; never clear entered input until the local copy is durable.

sources.title: Design help resources for seamless problem solving
sources.notes: In-product help guidance: just-in-case assistance that is easy to reach but never intrusive, contextual triggers at the moment of need, searchable and structured help content, and both self-service and expert-support paths.

sources.title: Copy gesture and clipboard failure on slow connections
sources.notes: Copy-action guidance: a copy gesture can expire while a slow round trip runs, so prepare the link before copying on the tap; a button that looks identical on success and failure leaves the person unsure whether copying worked.

sources.title: A practical guide to secure second-factor sign-in
sources.notes: Second-factor guidance: one-time recovery codes shown once at setup, each code usable once and removed after use, verification required before the second factor counts as enabled, and a manual-entry fallback when scanning fails.

sources.title: Grid pattern: editing and navigating inside a cell
sources.notes: Grid editing keyboard contract: Enter or a printable key enters edit mode, Enter commits, Escape restores navigation and may undo edits, and arrow keys move between cells while navigating but belong to the control inside the cell while editing.

sources.title: Timing an in-app rating prompt around success moments
sources.notes: Rating-prompt timing: ask right after a clear success moment and never during errors or onboarding friction, use the system review prompt and respect its frequency limits, suppress prompts for people with open support issues, and keep a feedback channel that does not block public reviews.

sources.title: Skip to main content links guide
sources.notes: Bypass links: first focusable element, hidden until focused, target accepts programmatic focus, focus moves rather than only scrolling, task-specific targets such as a checkout form on multi-step flows.

sources.title: Favorites design pattern: examples and best practices
sources.notes: Favorites as a one-action save for later return, with a saved list the person can return to; distinct from liking or sharing, which are lost in activity streams.

sources.title: Bulk actions UX: selection scope, confirmation, and partial failure
sources.notes: Bulk actions must state scope before execution and explain each outcome afterwards, especially partial failure where only some selected items succeed.

sources.title: Content reviews and content ratings
sources.notes: Star-based rating with an optional comment, one review per item, editing an existing review rather than adding a second, and moderation before publication.

sources.title: Toggle switch accessibility checklist
sources.notes: Switch placement by column width: switch beside the label on wide desktop columns so label and control stay visible together under magnification, switch on the right of the label on narrow columns; switches are for immediate on/off settings only, not for actions needing confirmation.

sources.title: Payment failure recovery: preserve the order, offer retry and fallback methods
sources.notes: Failed payments recover best inside the same checkout: preserve the order, retry only when the failure is clear, offer a relevant fallback method without a restart, and check the real status before any second attempt so no duplicate charge or order is created.

sources.title: Anchored comments: discussion attached to the content it discusses
sources.notes: Anchor each discussion thread to the specific section, sentence, or element it discusses so context travels with the comment; decide plainly what happens when the anchored text is deleted or heavily rewritten, and let thread visibility follow the visibility of the content itself.

sources.title: In-product update announcements: tiered visibility and a persistent entry point
sources.notes: Surface updates in context with action-oriented wording, a supporting visual, and a direct route to the new capability; grade visibility by impact so minor changes stay in the changelog while workflow-changing updates get a prominent, dismissible announcement and a persistent entry point for later review.

sources.title: Account and app switchers: design guidance
sources.notes: Account switchers show the active account plainly with signed-in alternatives and an add-account action; app switchers let a person jump between products in a suite while the navigation structure and information hierarchy stay familiar.

sources.title: Content reporting and blocking guidance
sources.notes: Reporting tools should remove the reported item from the reporter's view at once and block the reported party's content for the reporter even before review completes; batch reporting and severity options keep reporting usable.

sources.title: Language selector design guidance
sources.notes: Language names in their own language, no flags standing for languages, selector in a consistent place, keep the person on the same page on switching, suggest rather than force a detected language, always offer a way back.

sources.title: Scheduled message editing guidance
sources.notes: Scheduled messages stay visible with their scheduled time, remain editable or cancellable before sending, and editing content without changing the time keeps the original send time.

sources.title: Mobile faceted search guidance
sources.notes: On compact screens keep a sticky filter control with an active count, use a bottom sheet for a few facets and a full-screen panel for long lists, defer the list refresh until apply with a live result count on the apply control, and keep applied filters as removable chips.

sources.title: Faceted search best practices
sources.notes: Build facet counts from in-stock items and recalculate them after each selection, keep the filter control visible while scrolling, show a live result count on apply, and keep applied filters visible as removable chips.

sources.title: Breadcrumb navigation guidance
sources.notes: Breadcrumb as secondary navigation showing page position in a hierarchy; on narrow screens early levels collapse into a dropdown, the current page is not a link, and long labels use ellipsis.

sources.title: Breadcrumb design guidance
sources.notes: Breadcrumbs describe a tree while steppers describe a sequence; collapse on narrow screens rather than removing the trail, truncate carefully with full text available, and never rely on colour alone.

sources.title: Discussion comments guidance
sources.notes: Discussion threads can be resolved without deleting them, resolved threads stay viewable through a filter, and a resolved thread can be reopened.

sources.title: Dark-mode toggle guidance
sources.notes: A theme switcher that respects the system preference until an explicit choice is made, persists that choice, applies it before first paint to avoid a flash of the wrong theme, and exposes its state to assistive technology.

sources.title: Activity feed accessibility guidance
sources.notes: An activity feed should expose its timeline as a list so assistive technology reports item count and position, report how many events loading more adds, and let a reader find the collection, understand one item, request more, and continue without losing their place.

sources.title: Filter interface design guidance
sources.notes: Within one filter category selections combine as OR, while selections across categories combine as AND; long option lists offer search inside the category; applied filters stay visible as removable chips.

sources.title: Profile menu design guidance
sources.notes: Profile menu structure: clear concise labels, placement within thumb reach, account actions grouped apart from product navigation.

sources.title: Recently viewed pattern guidance
sources.notes: Recently viewed lists let people pick up where they left off; recents are recorded automatically, distinct from items deliberately saved.

sources.title: Meeting invitation response guidance
sources.notes: Accept, tentative, and decline replies with distinct calendar effects; a changed reply updates the invitation rather than duplicating it; deleting an invitation without replying leaves attendance unknown.

sources.title: Accessible interactive maps guidance
sources.notes: Dragging must not be the only way to pan, set a stop, or reorder a route; offer pan buttons, tap-to-place, an address field, and reorder controls, with keyboard panning, a documented focus exit, named zoom, locate, and close controls, and minimum target sizes.

sources.title: Intuitive barcode scanning interface guidance
sources.notes: Scanning interfaces stay clear and simple with a prominent scan action, a framing guide, visual and haptic capture feedback, and failure messages that suggest adjusting angle, distance, or light rather than a generic failure.

sources.title: Accessible QR code guidance
sources.notes: Codes shown to others need enough size, strong contrast, a glare-free surface, predictable placement, and plain-text instructions stating what scanning the code does.

sources.title: Modal dialog pattern guidance
sources.notes: Dialogs stay focused on one decision, with clear dismiss paths, focus taken on opening and returned on closing, focus trapped while open, and no nested dialogs.

sources.title: Guest checkout guidance
sources.notes: Guest checkout asks only for fulfilment details, offers account creation after payment, and keeps the receipt as the route to manage the order.

sources.title: Time-zone selector research findings
sources.notes: People search for zones by city rather than offset; selectors should identify the detected zone, offer search, organise alphabetically by city with country and offset shown.

sources.title: Coach mark guidance
sources.notes: Coach marks highlight one new or changed element at a time: appear on first reach of a feature, stay close to the target, carry a short benefit-focused note, allow dismissal, and appear once per session; prefer top or bottom placement with a centred caret.

sources.title: In-app updates guidance
sources.notes: Flexible updates download in the background while the person keeps working; immediate updates block use until installed, reserved for urgent cases; a grace period before enforcement keeps prompts from nagging.

sources.title: Accessibility settings guidance
sources.notes: A dedicated accessibility tab gathers text size, high contrast, reduced motion, sound captions, and control changes in one place, with layouts rearranging to fit larger text.

sources.title: Table of contents design guidance
sources.notes: A sticky table of contents stays reachable while scrolling, with the current section highlighted so readers know where they are; it needs a clear header so it is not confused with local navigation.

sources.title: Map interface design guidance
sources.notes: Choosing a place pairs a map with a list showing the same places; detail cards carry name, address, hours, and availability, and location-access failures keep area search available as the fallback.

sources.title: Pull-to-refresh pattern guidance
sources.notes: Pull-to-refresh refreshes lists sorted newest first; pulling shows a progress indicator, releasing before the threshold aborts, and the indicator spins until loading finishes.

sources.title: In-app update prompt design guidance
sources.notes: Update prompts graded by urgency: an optional banner first, then a once-a-day prompt, then a blocking prompt only before a hard cutoff, each stating the affected capability and the deadline in plain words.

sources.title: Table of contents and jump link guidance
sources.notes: A table of contents helps long pages when jump links move keyboard focus to the section heading and a sticky header never hides the heading after the jump; short pages and every-heading-level lists add clutter.

sources.title: Tabs design rules and failure cases
sources.notes: Scrollable tab strips scroll rather than wrap, show a hint of the next tab, snap so no tab rests half-cut, mark the current tab in text and shape, and use a consistent indicator on the edge touching the panel.

sources.title: Web share fallback and cancellation guidance
sources.notes: Where no share sheet exists, offer a fallback route such as a link or download; treat dismissal of the sheet as a normal outcome rather than an error.

sources.title: Find-in-document match count and navigation guidance
sources.notes: A find control shows the current match against the total, steps to the next and previous matches, and highlights all matches with the current one distinct.

sources.title: Find pattern in list, table, and card views
