sources.notes: Shared household lists with live sync; members claim items so nobody buys the same item twice; duplicate warnings; bought items kept in a separate section; changes by others stay visible on next open with an unseen-changes count; spend stats per participant and per product; receipt scan fills in weights and prices after checkout; saved templates for repeated lists.

sources.title: Zero-tap sign-in restoration for apps with sign-in, enforced from April 2027
sources.notes: Apps that support sign-in must restore the signed-in state on a new device when the person transfers data, using the restore-credentials flow; the requirement covers device-to-device transfer and cloud backup, applies whether sign-in is compulsory or optional, and excludes games for now, with exemptions possible for apps under strict security rules.

sources.title: Verified account badge: display rules, what the badge confirms, and when it must not appear
sources.notes: A verification badge shows only once a check is confirmed, never on cached or self-declared data; it states what was checked, uses the supplied mark unchanged, and is never shown for an unverified account.

sources.title: Background blur and replacement in video calls: privacy, attention, and when blur is not enough
sources.notes: Blurring a background keeps the person in focus while reducing distracting detail; replacing it with an image suits the tone of the meeting; blur hides detail, not movement, and sensitive items should still be moved out of frame.

sources.title: World clock and time-zone planning: shared timelines, working-hour bands, and sharing local times
sources.notes: Compare several time zones on one visual timeline with local times, dates, awake-hour and work-hour bands; swipe through the day to find work-hour overlap, adjust in small steps, and share a clear local-time summary for a chosen moment.

sources.title: Product questions and answers: moderated shopper questions with helpfulness votes on a product page
sources.notes: Approved questions on a product page shown newest first, each expanding to reveal its answer; an ask-a-question form with a short question field, optional contact and optional images; helpfulness votes on answers; the asker's own question marked as awaiting review until approved; guidance to work the moderation queue daily so unanswered questions do not linger.

sources.title: App Clips as lightweight app entry: single-task slices without a full install, and the end of the cross-platform equivalent
sources.notes: A small task-specific slice of an app opens in seconds from a code, tag, link, message, map listing, or search result, without installing the full app; it does one job (pay, order, book), shows a system card first, and offers a one-tap path to the full app after the task. The other major platform ended its equivalent no-install route in December 2025, leaving this a single-platform entry with a mobile-web fallback elsewhere.

sources.title: How to choose an online whiteboard tool for a remote team
sources.notes: Choosing a shared whiteboard by use: live workshops, retrospectives, diagramming, design feedback, and asynchronous sessions; core canvas checks are smooth pan and zoom with many objects, sticky notes, shapes with connectors that stay attached, and named frames to organise and jump between areas; collaboration checks are live cursors with names, a follow-the-facilitator view, timers, voting, hiding notes during silent brainstorming, and bringing everyone to one spot; templates, access levels for drawing and viewing, and export of the finished board.

sources.title: Collaborative cursors and presence API approach for accurate document editing
sources.notes: Presence, cursor motion, and document state need separate contracts: presence answers membership only; cursor packets are disposable and the latest coordinate wins; after a disconnect, mark the roster uncertain and replace it from a fresh snapshot rather than merging, so departed people never linger; undo reverses only the person's own edits.

sources.title: AusAlert active in the ACT from Sunday, 1 November 2026
sources.notes: Cell-broadcast emergency warnings: two tiers, with the highest tier sounding a siren-like tone and vibration even on silent or do-not-disturb settings and unable to be turned off; each warning states what the emergency is, where it is, how serious it is, what action to take, who issued it and where to find more; no registration, app or phone number needed, and a dismissed warning moves to the notification centre.

sources.title: How to reimburse employees for business expenses without the admin
sources.notes: Expense claim workflow: capture the receipt, amount, date, merchant, category and reason while details are fresh; require receipts and key details before submission; route claims to the right reviewer by team, value or category; states from submit through review, approval, payment and sync.

sources.title: Read state, unread and receipts
sources.notes: Message read states: sending, sent, delivered and read shown on the sender's own messages, with reader counts in groups; mark read when the latest message is reached with the conversation in front; mark unread moves the read position back; privacy controls stop sending read or delivery states.

sources.title: Live Chat Typing Indicators and Wait Messages: What to Show
sources.notes: Typing indicators as a promise that someone is working on a reply: show the indicator only while activity is real, stop it when activity stops, pair longer waits with a plain wait message and a time estimate, and never let a long-running indicator stand in for an absent reply.

sources.title: Waiting rooms in video meetings: why and how
sources.notes: Waiting-room mechanics: a holding view where joiners wait until the host admits them, with no sight or sound of the call until then; admit or decline by entered name, admit promptly, never admit a name that cannot be placed; ask-to-join when the call is at its limit; switch the waiting room off once everyone expected has arrived.

sources.title: The passkey UX patterns that drive adoption in 2026
sources.notes: Passkey adoption patterns: conditional mediation so passkeys appear in the username autofill dropdown, immediately available credentials as a fast path where sign-in intent is already clear, the Signal API to remove stale credentials from credential managers, and automatic upgrade of eligible password users to a passkey after a successful sign-in.

sources.title: Making search autocomplete accessible: the ARIA combobox pattern for e-commerce
sources.notes: Accessible search suggestions: focus stays in the input while arrowing through suggestions with the highlighted option announced as the current one, the suggestion count or a no-matches state announced as a status message without moving focus, and the panel open or closed state exposed to assistive technology.

sources.title: Schedule a Focus Mode
sources.notes: Focus mode schedules: named modes per activity with their own allowlists of people and apps, schedules by time, location, or app launch with days stated, a visible state while on, an automatic reply to senders, sync across devices, and separate exception lists per mode so a mode that allows everything is a label rather than a boundary.

sources.title: Toggle UX: switch, toggle button or checkbox — how to pick
sources.notes: Distinguishes toggle switch, toggle button and segmented control; a toggle button stays pressed for repeatable actions such as bold, mute or filter chips; the label names the function while the pressed state is announced separately; the pressed state is shown by shape and wording as well as colour; keyboard contract with visible focus.

sources.title: Use waiting rooms in Google Meet
sources.notes: Waiting room holds people outside the call until the host admits them; host admits one by one or brings everyone in, sends one-way messages to the waiting room, and can move someone back out; participants in the waiting room cannot see or hear the meeting.

sources.title: Messaging extensions
sources.notes: Sticker and messaging-extension guidance: design for expressiveness, use descriptive image names or alternative text labels so assistive technology can describe stickers, animate at a fluid frame rate, and keep each extension focused on a single purpose with an easy browse-and-select interface.

sources.title: Focus Mode on Phone and Computer: A Practical Setup Guide
sources.notes: Three modes with one set of rules: named modes with a small allowlist of people and apps, schedules by time, location or app, repeated calls breaking through, and notification summaries delivering held alerts in batches at set times.

sources.title: Paywall best practices for 2026: what the data says
sources.notes: Paywall structure: value-first headline, trial shown as a dated timeline with a reminder before the first charge, one plan pre-selected, and a single alternative offer when the person closes the first offer.

sources.title: 404 Page Best Practices: UX Design Tips & Inspiring Examples (2026)
sources.notes: Plain not-found statement without a bare error code, site header and navigation kept, a way back plus a search box, few choices, and a route to report the broken link.

sources.title: Navigation and the mobile menu: patterns
sources.notes: Bottom tab bar or a row under the header over a hidden burger; open menu puts search first, large rows, contacts at the bottom; header hides on scroll down and returns slimmer on scroll up; breadcrumbs shrink to one step back on a phone.

sources.title: Your CAPTCHA Might Violate WCAG 2.2 — Here's What an Accessible Alternative Looks Like
sources.notes: A puzzle must never be the only route: offer an alternative method or an assistance mechanism; object recognition is the permitted exception; invisible checks keep most people from ever seeing a challenge; a visual challenge needs an audio alternative and a plain next step after failure.

sources.title: Prepare your app for the resizability and orientation changes in Android 17
sources.notes: On wide screens the platform ignores orientation locks, resizability limits and aspect-ratio limits; layouts must work in both orientations and at any window aspect ratio; cap content width in wide landscape; keep primary actions reachable; re-measure preview surfaces on orientation change.

sources.title: Raise your hand in Google Meet
sources.notes: A raised hand is queued in order and shown on the tile and in the participants list; the moderator can lower one hand or all; speaking lowers the hand with a cancel step to keep it raised; gesture detection is off by default and raises the hand from a physical gesture.

sources.title: Disappearing messages
sources.notes: Each message carries its lifetime; expired messages are hidden from queries and deleted from local storage; disappearing messages need a distinct visual style and a visible countdown so people know the message will vanish.

sources.title: Tips on how to collaborate in a video meeting
sources.notes: Breakout rooms split a meeting into smaller groups with a return to the main call; the host assigns rooms and controls who can create them; breakout rooms cannot be live streamed or recorded.

sources.title: What is a scrolling window manager?
sources.notes: A scrolling window manager lines windows up as columns on a horizontal strip wider than the screen; opening a window adds a column without shrinking the others, and moving focus slides the strip until the wanted column is visible, so each column keeps the width it was given. Tiling fits every window on screen and shrinks them as more open; scrolling keeps every window usable at the cost of not seeing them all at once.

sources.title: Screen Sharing Privacy Checklist Before a Call
sources.notes: Share one window instead of the whole screen; turn on Do Not Disturb, close private tabs, check the preview before confirming, and stop sharing from the call controls before opening private content.

sources.title: How to mute or unmute individual or group chat notifications
sources.notes: Mute one conversation for 8 hours, 1 week, or always; messages still arrive and stay readable on opening, and the mute carries across the phone, web, and desktop.

sources.title: How to Send Messages That Automatically Disappear
sources.notes: Per-conversation timers from seconds to weeks, with the count starting when a message is seen; a screenshot or a second device can keep a copy, and some apps notify the sender when a screenshot is taken.

sources.title: Automotive UX (IVI, Clusters & Driver-Facing Design)
sources.notes: Head-up displays show speed, the next manoeuvre, and critical warnings only; overlays stay fixed to what they annotate and never cover hazards or sightlines; about two seconds per glance and about twelve seconds per task.

sources.title: Wearables and Smartwatch Design (watchOS, Wear OS)
sources.notes: One question per glance and one screen per job; a short look followed by a longer look with actions if the wrist stays raised; context-triggered suggestions surface the relevant item at the right moment; the ambient variant never shows sensitive detail.

sources.title: Pre-Purchase vs In-Cart vs Post-Purchase Upsells: Shopify Surfaces in 2026
sources.notes: Where each offer belongs: pre-purchase, in-cart, and post-purchase surfaces compared; one offer per surface, relevance to what is already chosen, a price small beside the order total, and no extra decision step inside payment.

sources.title: Chatbot UI Examples (2026): 12 Patterns From Real Products
sources.notes: Long outputs belong beside the conversation rather than buried in it; citations are shown as first-class interface elements; suggested changes are reviewed before they apply; the route to a person is designed as a feature, not a failure.

sources.title: Language detection and localization guidance
sources.notes: Starting language follows the saved preference first, then the browser or device language; place is never used to infer language; an unavailable detected language is stated up front with a choice offered; language names are written in their own language and never replaced by a flag.

sources.title: Multi-step form and wizard UX patterns
sources.notes: Group steps by meaning with the fewest steps that keep each one focused; the progress indicator reflects the real remaining effort, not just the screen count, and a branching path shows its conditional route instead of a percentage; named steps beat bare numbers; data persists on back navigation and focus moves to the new step heading.

sources.title: SaaS Data Table & List View UX Patterns (2026)
sources.notes: Data table as a working surface: five or six identifying columns with the rest in detail view or optional columns; sticky headers and first column; sorting and row selection as core interactions; right-aligned numbers with consistent decimals; a totals row pinned in the footer; density toggle; horizontal scroll or stacked cards on narrow screens.

sources.title: Meeting recording consent and notice guidance
sources.notes: Participants must be told in advance why a call is recorded, how the recording is handled, where it is stored, and how long it is kept; a visible recording indicator stays on for the whole call, and people can decline or join without being recorded.

sources.title: Receiving calls design guidance
sources.notes: An incoming call arrives as a notice with the caller's name or number and answer and decline controls; the notice persists until the call is answered, declined, or missed; answering a second call during a call puts the first call on hold with switch and merge options.

sources.title: Missed call follow-up plan
sources.notes: A missed call needs a defined next action: who owns the follow-up, a realistic deadline, and a recorded outcome for each return attempt; a failed callback is a task, not a closed enquiry, and repeated calls from one caller are treated as one thread.

sources.title: Guide for Mobile Text Scaling
sources.notes: Text must scale to 200% without loss of content or function: use the platform scaling units, let containers expand, keep every text element inside a scroll view, and avoid fixed heights and widths on text containers.

sources.title: User Experience Design Guidelines for Merchant-Presented Codes
sources.notes: Scan-to-pay needs two modes: scanning a code shown by the seller, or showing a personal code for the seller to scan. A code carrying a fixed amount shows it up front; a static code asks the person to enter the amount. A shown code stays large and high-contrast on a plain background, with a full-screen option on small screens, and fills most of the scan frame at a normal holding distance.

sources.title: Design an Unforgettable Splash Screen for Your Users
sources.notes: Platform guidance for launch screens: keep the screen only as long as loading takes, never add artificial delays, keep content minimal with no text or advertising; one approach mirrors the first screen without branding, the other shows a centred brand mark on a plain background with an optional entry animation.

sources.title: Design Forms to Prevent Mistakes
sources.notes: Choose a form design that reduces the chance of a mistake: ask for as little as possible, accept as many input formats as possible, divide long numbers into chunks with autocomplete across fields, correct errors automatically only when reliable, and offer known suggestions and corrections.

sources.title: SaaS Destructive Actions & Confirmation UX Patterns (2026)
sources.notes: Scale the friction to the blast radius: no confirmation for free actions, a light confirmation for restorable deletions, an explicit-consequence confirmation for irreversible actions, and type-to-confirm for the highest-stakes actions; prefer undo over confirmation where the action is reversible, and keep the undo visible long enough to be noticed.

sources.title: Call statuses and what they mean
sources.notes: Outbound call stages in order: queued, initiated, ringing, in-progress, completed; final states where a call never connects are busy, no-answer, cancelled, and failed, with failed meaning the destination could not be reached, often because the number was entered wrongly or is unreachable.

sources.title: Connection unstable guidance for video calls
sources.notes: Warn only when connection quality is poor, to avoid warning fatigue; show the warning to the person whose own connection is poor, since they can act on it; when the connection drops, reconnect automatically and show a small indicator for a brief interruption and a fuller reconnecting view when the drop lasts.

sources.title: Use web content within your Android app
sources.notes: Use an embedded view only for web content the app controls; use the platform in-app browser for links that should keep the person in the app; use the system browser for sign-in to another service so credentials stay isolated. A web view that leads onward needs forward and back navigation enabled with controls to use it.

sources.title: Cancellation flows: how to save subscribers without trapping them
sources.notes: Cancellation flow anatomy: easy to find, one reason question, one relevant alternative matched to the reason and shown once, declining as easy as accepting, no repeated offers, clear exit with written confirmation; pause as the most underused alternative.

sources.title: Notification Inbox UX: Read, Done, and Unsubscribe Explained
sources.notes: Notification inbox triage: read, done, and following are separate dimensions — reading never resolves, done removes from the active queue without changing read state, following controls future updates; badge counts unread threads in the active queue excluding done items; unsubscribe consequences stated plainly.

sources.title: Activity rings are harder to read than bar charts
sources.notes: Review of goal-progress display research: bar charts read faster and with fewer errors than radial ring displays for goal-progress checks on a small screen; rings suit a glanceable summary; missed-goal framing matters more than whether the miss is shown.

sources.title: Set up Voicemail on iPhone
sources.notes: Visual voicemail shows recorded messages as a list with caller, time, and length, playable and deletable in any order; written transcripts are labelled as transcripts and depend on recording quality; Live Voicemail shows a real-time transcript as a message is being left, with a pick-up option; an unheard-message count and carrier and region availability are stated.

sources.title: Video conferencing providers to include accessibility features
sources.notes: Live captions in video calls must be accurate and synchronous, with user controls for size, font, position, and the colour and opacity of captions and background; third-party captioning services connect and display on the same call screen; sign-language interpretation from third parties is supported, with the interpreter pinnable beside the speaker.

sources.title: A Smartphone Safety Check Offers Peace of Mind
sources.notes: Timed and destination-based safety check-ins: choose a reason and a duration or destination, choose trusted contacts, optionally tell them when the check-in starts, add time while it runs, confirm safety at the end of the chosen time, and alert the contacts with the last known position if there is no answer inside a short response window; a limited data-sharing level passes only position, battery level, and signal strength, while a fuller level adds the route and the last places the device was used.

sources.title: How to use Breakout Rooms
sources.notes: Breakout rooms split one meeting into smaller sessions: the host creates rooms and assigns participants automatically, manually, or lets them choose their own room; participants can return to the main session at any time where allowed, and a countdown runs after rooms are closed before everyone is returned; late joiners are assigned on arrival; the host can broadcast messages to all rooms and join rooms.

sources.title: Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) Call Control - Transfer
sources.notes: Call transfer services include blind transfer, consultative transfer, and attended transfer: in a blind transfer the call is passed on without first speaking to the recipient; in a consultative transfer the caller is held while the transferor speaks to the recipient; in an attended transfer the recipient is briefed and the transfer completes with the caller joined to the new leg; recovery returns the transferor to the caller where the recipient cannot be reached.

sources.title: (Blind) Users Really Do Heed Aural Telephone Scam Warnings
sources.notes: A study of aural telephone scam warnings with blind and sighted participants: contextual warnings that state what the scam is about work as usable security cues together with verification indicators such as a scam-likely label; labels can be wrong, so a warning must state its reason and never decide for the person; warnings must be spoken as well as shown so they reach people who cannot see the screen.

sources.title: Digital identity wallet technical specifications: user experience design
sources.notes: Technical specification for a national digital identity wallet, section 5 on user experience design: before presenting, the person reviews the requested data, the requesting service and its policy, chooses which non-mandatory items to share, consents or cancels, authorises with the wallet unlock method, and receives confirmation; in-person presentation shows a scannable code for the verifier, in supervised or unsupervised modes.

sources.title: Game Accessibility Guidelines: basic set
sources.notes: Community guidelines for making games playable by more people, organised by barrier type and effort level: large well-spaced interactive elements, every part of the interface reachable with the same input used for play, remappable controls, readable default text sizes, high contrast between text or interface and background, no essential information by colour alone, adjustable font size and contrast, resizable interfaces, subtitles presented clearly, and speech input only as a supplement.

sources.title: Text display in games: minimum sizes and scaling
sources.notes: Platform accessibility guidance on text display in games: minimum default text sizes by device class, text in menus, heads-up display elements, objectives and chat, icons and glyphs scaling with text up to 200 percent, and text over changing backgrounds measured against its lowest-contrast area.

sources.title: Screen your calls before you answer them
sources.notes: Platform guidance on call screening: the phone answers an unknown call and asks who is calling and why, shows a live transcript on the incoming-call screen, offers suggested replies and a route to ask the caller another question, ends the call on its own where the caller is unwanted, keeps screened-call transcripts on the device, and uses saved contacts to decide which calls to screen.

sources.title: Banking app design: principles, examples and UX best practices (2026)
sources.notes: Banking onboarding and identity verification: show step count and remaining steps before document upload or selfie verification, give framing and lighting guidance for document capture, explain why an image cannot be verified, replace indefinite loading with a review status, realistic timing and a save-and-return path, summarise required terms with the full text available on demand, and give a plain-language reason plus retry or save-and-return where verification fails. Transaction history: readable merchant labels, search and filters, a visible difference between pending, completed, reversed, and disputed operations, detail views exposing the payment method, reference number, and dispute path, and sensitive data masked by default with a deliberate reveal action.

sources.title: Keyboard Navigation Patterns for Complex Widgets: A Complete ARIA Guide (2026)
sources.notes: Keyboard navigation for complex widgets following WAI-ARIA practices: Tab moves between widgets while arrow keys move within, Enter and Space activate, Escape dismisses; modal dialogs move focus inside on opening, cycle Tab within, keep background content inert, and return focus to the trigger on closing; the native dialog element supplies these behaviours without custom code.

sources.title: Human interface guidelines comparison, early 2025 to September 2026
sources.notes: Dated comparison of platform guideline pages: new Snippets guidance for concise system-mediated views; confirmation and result presentations have different jobs; complex detail leads into the app rather than overflowing the lightweight surface.

sources.title: Contactless transit fare payment guidance
sources.notes: Fare-capped day pass after the second payment of the day; the same card must be used for every tap; a physical card and the same card in a wallet count as different methods; the fare is shown on the reader after the tap; charges appear on the bank or card statement with a possible temporary hold.

sources.title: Tap on, tap off tram fares
sources.notes: Tap on before boarding and tap off when leaving; daily and weekly caps calculated from journeys made; a missed tap-off charges the highest fare and does not count towards the cap; the same card or device must be used throughout; an inspection tap checks the fare was paid.

sources.title: Remote-control navigation for TV web apps
sources.notes: Row-and-column grid navigation over nearest-element navigation; focus obvious from across the room; the focused row held steady on screen; rows slid with transforms rather than scrolling the document.

sources.title: Navigation on TV
sources.notes: Directional pad as the primary navigation method; every visible control reachable without touch; the back button returns to the previous destination; categories on the vertical axis, items within a category on the horizontal axis.

sources.title: Guideline for Incorporating Human Factors in Human Machine Interface
sources.notes: 54 human-factors principles across 14 design criteria for in-vehicle systems, covering device placement, interaction methods, and restricted functions; applies to light and heavy vehicles.

sources.title: Honk if you want your car's physical buttons back
sources.notes: Revised 2026 safety-rating protocols require physical controls for indicators, wipers, hazard lights, horn, and emergency call; touchscreen-only cars score poorly on primary driving controls; physical controls allow operation without extended attention away from the road.

sources.title: Deceptive design patterns in social media platform interfaces: how to recognise and avoid them — Guidelines 03/2022, version 2.0
sources.notes: Six deceptive design pattern categories — overloading, skipping, stirring, obstructing, fickle, left in the dark — with concrete examples per use case and best practices: objective neutral presentation, least invasive option as the default, shortcuts and bulk options to data settings.

sources.title: Criteria for websites (from end of 2026)
sources.notes: Version 4.1.1 of the European harmonised standard for ICT accessibility, published 2 September 2026, expected to be cited in the Official Journal by late November 2026 and to replace version 3.2.1; web and software clauses move to WCAG 2.2 A and AA, with the criteria summarised from the final draft.

sources.title: Overview of Accessibility Nutrition Labels
sources.notes: Store listing section declaring which accessibility features an app supports: nine labels, a feature claimed only where every common task can be completed with it, support declared per device, section shown even where support is undeclared or none, optional link to accessibility details, and labels used in search relevance.

sources.title: Guidelines for Accessibility in PIN Entry on Touchscreen Terminals
sources.notes: Payments industry accessibility guidelines for PIN entry on touchscreen terminals, December 2019: fixed telephone keypad layout with 5 central, tactile keypad alternative with raised marker on 5, haptic and audio feedback by count only with no digit-identifying variation, never display or announce any digit, assisted-entry mode with several activation routes and spoken amount, progress and outcome, and amount stated before entry.

sources.title: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce
sources.notes: Adopted 17 January 2023: no reject option on the first layer, pre-ticked boxes, reject as a link without visual support, deceptive button colours and contrast, a basis other than consent claimed for cookie purposes, inaccurately classified essential cookies, and no withdraw icon — the common positions on cookie banner practices.

sources.title: Public Charge Point Regulations 2023 guidance
sources.notes: Contactless payment without a prior contract, price per unit of energy shown before the session, price fixed once charging starts, a staffed telephone helpline, and open availability and pricing data.

sources.title: Alternative fuel infrastructure requirements
sources.notes: Payment and accessibility requirements for publicly funded charge points, including contactless payment and clear pricing.

sources.title: How to create an accessible EV bay
sources.notes: Summary of the accessibility specification for charge points: bay layout, control heights, cable weight, screen and interface provision, and digital platforms.

sources.title: Device controls
sources.notes: Quick-access controls for connected home devices: templated control widgets, device state shown on the tile, and controls grouped by device.

sources.title: Travel accommodations audit
sources.notes: Independent usability audit of travel accommodation sites across search, property, room selection and checkout, with 400+ weighted parameters; room-and-rate comparison findings.

sources.title: Hotel rate plans and the room selection page
sources.notes: Name each rate by its consequences with the cancellation deadline in the label, identical attributes in identical order on every rate card, and the price difference stated as a trade-off.

sources.title: Onboarding and connecting smart devices: five guidelines for user-friendly smart-device apps
sources.notes: Visual step-by-step setup with one task at a time, expected device responses stated in advance, reconnection treated like first-time setup, honest progress indicators, transparent error handling, and naming the device before finishing.

sources.title: UI placement as a critical design factor for augmented reality during locomotion
sources.notes: Workshop paper on interface placement while walking: world-fixed and path-following placements give the steadiest gaze, head-locked placement the least steady, head-following with a delay in between.

sources.title: UI design guidance for AR spectacles
sources.notes: Additive display colour space, three-dimensional forms for interactive elements with flat planes for text, motion and spatial audio for attention guidance.

sources.title: QR code payment specifications
sources.notes: Merchant-presented and consumer-presented QR payment modes; the code carries merchant identity, amount and currency in a structured format; a specific authenticated app is generally required to process the payment data.

sources.title: Key behaviours guidance for fundraisers
sources.notes: Online fundraising: fees clear to donors before payment details are requested; fundraising open, honest, respectful and legal; donors able to make an informed decision and ask for more information.

sources.title: Guidelines for regulating shared micromobility
sources.notes: Shared micromobility regulation: designated parking near trip ends, fleet size, customer-service expectations, safety provisions, and data standards.

sources.title: Micromobility sharing schemes operating authorisation guide
sources.notes: Operator conditions for shared micromobility schemes including accessibility, parking, and service-area rules (October 2026).

sources.title: Shared micromobility accessibility
sources.notes: Bikeshare and scooter-share apps, websites and docking stations usable by people with disabilities: audio cues, braille labels, large print; devices must not obstruct sidewalks.

sources.title: Using video conferencing and consultation tools
sources.notes: Video consultations: confirm the patient is in a safe, quiet, confidential place; confirm who else is in the room on both sides; confirm identity; keep a phone fallback.

sources.title: Flowchart 2: Conducting high-quality telephone or video consultations
sources.notes: Test technology before the consultation; bring up the patient record and phone number in case video fails; confirm audio and visual quality at the start; clinician confirms own identity and verifies patient identity; agree the phone fallback; summarise next steps at the close.

sources.title: Videoconference consultation considerations
sources.notes: Begin by introducing name and role; identity check; confirm the participant's current location and best contact number in case of escalation; explain the process and what happens next.

sources.title: Media production standards for exhibits
sources.notes: Exhibit media produced with signed interpretation, captioning, descriptive audio track and transcription; versions in both official languages; standardised player with captions and sign language toggleable separately; volume control.

sources.title: Share a digital car key
sources.notes: Share a key held in a wallet with a named recipient; guest, co-owner and service access levels with expiry and reshare control; activation on first use; remove a shared key per recipient; transfer a key to a new device by scanning a code.

sources.title: About Digital Key
sources.notes: Share a key with named recipients through the wallet; sharing by QR code uses preset access options that cannot be changed; a lock-only key does not permit starting; the owner removes shared keys, each recipient removes only their own.

sources.title: How to Pick Up Your Parcel from an InPost Locker
sources.notes: Collect with a QR code or a collection code, or open the locker from the app; three-day collection window with a reminder at 24 hours left and return to sender after expiry; several parcels may share one compartment; an easy-access compartment can be requested.

sources.title: The Pickup Code: How Parcel Lockers and Stations Shape China's Delivery Culture
sources.notes: Six-digit pickup code sent by text with a stated expiry; enter the code at the locker screen or scan a QR code and the compartment opens; code is single-use; staffed station variant hands the parcel over on the last four digits of the phone number.

sources.title: How smart rings solve the UX challenges of screenless design
sources.notes: Screenless sensor devices: the ring is a passive sensor and the phone app carries the whole interface; daily scores for sleep, readiness, and activity with a plain-language reason and next step; a short check-in pairs measured data with how the person feels; haptics carry only intensity, duration, rhythm, and pattern, reserved for health alerts; minimal on-device gestures mapped to phone actions.

sources.title: Set up eSIM on iPhone
sources.notes: Activate a mobile plan on a built-in SIM by QR code, carrier app, carrier-assigned plan, transfer from a nearby phone, or typed details; convert a physical SIM on the same phone; transfer deactivates the plan on the old phone; several numbers can move at once.

sources.title: How to Switch eSIM Providers or Carriers, Step by Step
sources.notes: Switching takes a fresh plan from the new carrier rather than moving the old one; keep the number by porting it and do not cancel the old plan first; check the phone is unlocked and supports a built-in SIM; keep the old SIM until the new plan shows signal.

sources.title: Speech interactions
sources.notes: Speech for text input ranges from short form under 10 seconds to long-form dictation sessions up to two minutes; a microphone glyph shows that speech input is available and its state; continuous recognition ends when the connection is unavailable; supported responses shown where space permits.

sources.title: Voice Input UI: Design Better Real-World Workflows
sources.notes: Seven voice input states: idle, permission request, listening, paused, processing, success, error; keep the text field so the transcript can be read, corrected by typing, and submitted through the usual action; interim text appears while listening and final text becomes editable.

sources.title: Design for AI Glasses
sources.notes: Platform guidance for glasses: audio glasses use hands-free natural-language interaction with concise spoken responses and text to speech, where the same app states trigger spoken output; display glasses combine audio with subtle, glanceable, high-contrast, minimal visuals that appear only when relevant to enhance, not obstruct, the view; simplified theme for visibility on glasses.

sources.title: Add or delete guest
sources.notes: Create a temporary guest profile for sharing a phone; an option clears all data and apps installed during the session when the guest finishes, and exiting the guest session returns to the owner's profile.

sources.title: Shared device mode and guest temporary sessions
sources.notes: Temporary guest sessions on a shared tablet: local data is destroyed when the guest signs out, a message states that data will not be saved after signing out, and an optional timeout signs the guest out automatically.

sources.title: How live auctions work
sources.notes: One-tap bid for the next step above the current price; a maximum bid that bids in steps up to the stated cap and never past it; a sudden-death clock that tops back up on every bid and drops to 5 seconds at last call; the server clock decides the winner; every bid is a binding offer to buy.

sources.title: How to Run an Online Auction — Complete Operator's Guide
sources.notes: Bid increment chart that sets how much each next bid must rise; timed online auctions with anti-sniping logic extending the close by 1-5 minutes on a late bid and staggered lot closing; live sales simulcast online with latency between the rostrum and online bidders.

sources.title: Adding value to a Clipper card
sources.notes: Add value from a phone wallet or the app; auto-reload when the balance falls below a stated amount or on a weekly or monthly schedule; cash value held on a card is limited, and an order that would pass the limit cannot be loaded.

sources.title: Auto top-up for a go card
sources.notes: Auto top-up when the balance falls below $5, with a minimum top-up of $20; the first setup takes payment at once, and the value loads on the next tap, up to 60 minutes later.

sources.title: Airline Information and Entertainment Access Act: one-pager and section-by-section summary
sources.notes: Requires a captioning option on videos showing safety information and entertainment, a signed-language option, audio descriptions, and a nonvisual operating option for video display controls; the access board must prescribe standards for display controls.

sources.title: Flying with hearing loss could soon get easier
sources.notes: The 2024 aviation reauthorisation law requires the transport department to issue regulations on in-flight entertainment accessibility, including closed captioning and video descriptions; airport gates, counters, and ticketing areas must be accessible, including captions.

sources.title: Best Practices in Implementing Self Check-in Solutions
sources.notes: Industry guide for self check-in in hotels: a four-stage traveller journey (pre-register, arrival instructions, arrive and activate key, enter room), with design principles for kiosk and mobile self check-in, identity verification, and key handover.

sources.title: Kiosk Experience - Self-Service Kiosk
sources.notes: Kiosk-native hotel arrival flow: reservation lookup, the check-in steps the property allows, key issue at the end, and a completion screen that resets for the next guest; document capture handed to the guest's own phone by scannable code; language chosen on the device.

sources.title: Tenant Portal UX: Design That Residents Actually Use
sources.notes: Design guidance for resident portals citing renter-preference surveys: portal access and maintenance as the main drivers of satisfaction, phone-first design, push-plus-pull notifications with deep links into the portal for the action itself, and a visible login in primary navigation.

sources.title: How to Set Up a Tenant Portal (And Why Your Tenants Expect One in 2026)
sources.notes: Feature checklist for tenant portals: rent payment with autopay, maintenance submission with status tracking, payment history and receipts, lease and document access, and reminders before rent is due.

sources.title: QR Table Ordering: What Changes, What to Check
sources.notes: Independent review of QR order-and-pay at the table: one code per table opening the menu with the table already known, no app to install, split checks, a call-staff route, a stated check that the code on the table is genuine, and web accessibility guidance for the menu page behind the code.

sources.title: QR Code Ordering System for Restaurants
sources.notes: End-to-end table ordering flow: scan, browse with modifiers, order to the kitchen by table number, pay on the phone or at the end, call staff from the same screen; paper menu and staff kept available, and the system does not work during an internet outage.

sources.title: Designing for Disconnection: Creating Digital Products That Promote Well-being
sources.notes: Design principles for digital wellbeing: native dashboards showing daily and weekly use, soft limits that gently nudge when self-allotted time is up, focus modes that strip away non-essential elements, and clear stopping points instead of endless content.

sources.title: How to Reduce Screen Time (Ultimate Guide)
sources.notes: Cross-platform guide to screen-time controls: per-app daily limits with blocking at the end of the limit, scheduled downtime with allowed essentials, focus presets for work, family, and driving, and weekly usage reports.

sources.title: Accessing and sharing health records FAQs
sources.notes: Parliamentary research briefing: who may access a health record, proxy access with consent, sharing between professionals for direct care, and retention periods.

sources.title: How patient records are stored, used and shared
sources.notes: Hospital privacy notice: records shared only with professionals involved in direct care, retention of at least eight years, and the right to object to sharing.

sources.title: E-book apps and their typography
sources.notes: Reading-app typography: letter and line spacing carry the strongest evidence, shorter lines reduce place-keeping errors, and ragged-right keeps word spacing even on narrow screens.

sources.title: Accessible Typography: Choosing Readable Fonts
sources.notes: Accessible typography: 16px minimum body size, line height around 1.5, line length 45-75 characters, left-aligned text, and contrast of at least 4.5:1.

sources.title: EReader Apps And Low Vision Accessibility
sources.notes: Survey of mainstream e-reader apps for low-vision readers: adjustable text size, page colours, and layout customisation compared across apps and platforms.

sources.title: 2.2 Ballot Design
sources.notes: Open-textbook chapter on ballot design: what a ballot must state, candidate order effects, marking methods including ranked choice, and the cost of confusing layouts.

sources.title: Ranked choice voting
sources.notes: Best practices for ranked-choice ballot design, voter education, and results displays, based on usability testing of ballot layouts.

sources.title: The Usability of Ranked-Choice Voting in Digital Ballot Formats
sources.notes: Study of three digital ranked-choice ballot formats: bubble grid, column, and hand-numbered; hand-numbered was slowest with the most errors, bubble grid rated most usable.

sources.title: EU complaint form under Regulation (EC) 261/2004
sources.notes: National enforcement body complaint form for flight disruption: entitlement check, flight and booking details, compensation tiers by distance, and escalation where the carrier does not answer.

sources.title: How to File an EU261 Claim Yourself: Step-by-Step
sources.notes: Claim flow in order: check entitlement, find the airline claim form, write the claim with flight, delay, and distance stated, keep a copy and a case reference, and escalate to the national enforcement body after six weeks without a response; compensation tiers of 250, 400, and 600 by flight distance.

sources.title: Digital car key UX design guidelines (platform documentation)
sources.notes: Phone as car key: discovery and setup, locks and unlocks, phone controls, key sharing with access levels and expiry, proximity unlock with a visible signal and a notification; works without a cellular signal.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2019/882 on the accessibility requirements for products and services
sources.notes: Self-service terminals in scope: payment terminals, automated teller machines, ticketing machines, check-in machines, and interactive self-service terminals providing information. Terminal duties: text-to-speech, personal headsets, time limits warned through more than one sense with a way to extend them, adequate contrast and tactilely discernible keys and controls where keys are present, accessibility features that can be switched on without already needing them, and compatibility with hearing aids and telecoils where audio is used.

sources.title: Get classroom email summaries (for guardians)
sources.notes: A teacher or school administrator invites a guardian; the invitation must be accepted within 120 days. Summaries cover missing work, upcoming work, and class activities, and do not include grades. Guardians choose daily or weekly summaries, can unsubscribe or remove themselves at any time, and cannot access the classroom directly.

sources.title: Manage captions and translations in Chrome
sources.notes: Live Caption generates captions for audio in the browser; captions are processed locally, never stored, and never leave the device. Live Translate sends captions for translation, from a listed set of source languages to over 100 target languages. Both are switched on under Settings, Accessibility, Audio and captions.

sources.title: A User-Friendly Redesign of Departure Monitors in Local Public Transportation Based on a Comparative Eye Tracking Study
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed conference paper, first online 31 October 2026: a survey of 509 passengers and an eye-tracking study with 16 participants comparing a current departure-monitor layout with a redesigned one. The redesign keeps the board static, groups departures by transport kind, shows bus and tram times as countdowns and train times as clock times, states delays as added minutes, and codes disruptions in shape and words as well as colour, grounded in published legibility, contrast, and rail-accessibility standards.

sources.title: Decide when and where to get care (care cards)
sources.notes: Public design-system pattern guidance, updated August 2026 and re-tested in 2026: three cards for three urgency tiers, routine, urgent and emergency, each with one action heading followed by a short symptom list; urgency stated in words in the heading, never by colour alone; one signposted service per heading; cards ordered by likelihood and seriousness; only the emergency route in an emergency card.

sources.title: Chapter 3: Operable Parts
sources.notes: Regulator guidance on operable parts: reach range 15 to 48 inches above the floor for an unobstructed forward or side approach, reduced where reaching over an obstruction; clear floor space for approach; operable with one hand without tight grasping, pinching, or twisting of the wrist and with no more than 5 pounds of force.

sources.title: Chapter 7: Communication Elements and Features
sources.notes: Regulator standards for signs: raised characters 1/32 inch above the background, uppercase, sans serif, 5/8 inch to 2 inches high, duplicated in contracted Braille directly below the text, mounted with the baseline 48 to 60 inches above the floor on the latch side of the door; visual characters sized to viewing distance and mounted at least 40 inches above the floor; non-glare finish with strong light-on-dark or dark-on-light contrast.

sources.title: Investigating Essential Usability Factors of Online Course Registration Systems
sources.notes: Questionnaire study of two live course registration systems against ISONORM 9241/10: the systems differed most on self-descriptiveness and conformity with user expectations; labels and steps must explain what a control does and what happens next without prior training.

sources.title: Usability Evaluation of Class Enrolment Application for University Students
sources.notes: 2025 usability evaluation of a class enrolment application for university students: consistent course-listing structure so a planned timetable can be scanned and compared at a glance, and errors surfaced while planning so clashes, missing prerequisites, and full sections are fixed before the registration window opens.

sources.title: Course Registration Systems: Importance of Subjective Data in Interpretations of Usability
sources.notes: 22-participant experiment on error recovery in course registration: error messages should lead directly to the fix, and recovery should be measured, not only task time, since stress rises measurably after failed attempts.

sources.title: Donation Usability: Increasing Online Giving
sources.notes: Usability study of 23 non-profit sites: only 43% answered what the work is on the homepage and 4% answered how donations are used; on 17% of sites users could not find where to donate; the donation flow itself was largely usable, the content was the problem.

sources.title: Code of Fundraising Practice: table of changes
sources.notes: Regulator code of fundraising practice, effective 1 November 2025: donors must be treated fairly, not misled, and not pressured into regular giving; recurring terms and the route to cancel or amend must be stated plainly.

sources.title: How to Collect Donor Authorization for Direct Payment
sources.notes: Payments-standards guidance on donor authorisation for direct payment: state the amount, date of first payment, and interval in full at the point of commitment, and keep authorisation records for at least two years after cancellation.

sources.title: What's new in Wallet
sources.notes: Wallet pass updates: a poster-style pass face, four new barcode types, and up to two featured actions drawn below the pass face.

sources.title: Electronic signature
sources.notes: Public design-system pattern for signing a document online: guidance about signing placed in the journey before the signing step, and a check that the signer understands a ticked box carries the same effect as a handwritten signature.

sources.title: List and show a rental unit
sources.notes: Government guidance for landlords on rental listings: informative listings answering the renter's questions, photos of every room, pre-screening, and the essentials of a tenant application — verifiable income and employment, references, identification shown but not copied, credit check only with written approval — with the same documented criteria for every applicant.

sources.title: Rules of Operation — rental agencies
sources.notes: Municipal code for rental agencies: listings must be accurate and current, with availability verified at least once every 48 hours.

sources.title: A Guide to Insurance Claims
sources.notes: Regulator guide to making an insurance claim: notify as soon as practical, ask what is needed, how much time there is to file, and how long processing takes; claim reference number; acknowledgement within three working days; assessor visit within three working days; settlement windows by claim size.

sources.title: Getting ready for Self Assessment — a 10 point step-by-step guide
sources.notes: Government guidance on filing a tax return: eligibility check, registration, gathering figures first, saving progress and returning later, one step at a time, checking before submitting, and amending after submission.

sources.title: Structuring a service
sources.notes: Government design-system guidance on structuring an online service: one thing per page, and a chance to check answers before submitting.

sources.title: Telehealth Behavior Consultations Scheduling Checklist
sources.notes: Professional-association checklist for scheduling remote veterinary consultations: history form sent ahead, deposit to secure the appointment, video invite by email and text, a second contact route, and a medical summary from the primary clinician.

sources.title: Telemedicine Appointments
sources.notes: University veterinary hospital policy for telemedicine appointments: scheduled only with clinician approval, only for patients with an established care relationship, thirty-minute slots, and the fee stated when booking.

sources.title: Fulfillment
sources.notes: Platform handbook on fulfilling a crowdfunded project: no more than five reward tiers for a first project, the fulfilment plan explained in the risks section, backer surveys sent when shipping approaches, and an update to backers at the first sign of a roadblock.

sources.title: Cyber Security for Consumer Internet of Things: Requirements for Residential Smart Door Locking Devices (TS 103 815 V1.1.1)
sources.notes: Standards-body technical specification for residential smart door locking devices; its use-case annex names temporary access for guests, single-use access for deliveries or service, a list of users with authorised periods, and adding or removing a single user, and states that digital credentials can be sent between users, can carry date and time schedules, and can be revoked when lost or no longer trusted.

sources.title: Selling car rental: complying with consumer law
sources.notes: Regulator guidance for selling car rental: the headline price must include all compulsory charges including fuel and age surcharges, out-of-hours and one-way fees, and taxes; the fuel policy must be stated; the excess and any deposit or pre-authorisation must be stated clearly and prominently, no more than one click from the headline price.

sources.title: Code of Best Practice for the Car and Van Short Term Hire Industry
sources.notes: Industry code of best practice for short-term hire: the quoted price includes all mandatory charges; a pre-rental inspection report with a diagram notes pre-existing damage for the customer to check and agree before accepting; a post-rental inspection in the customer's presence produces a written report signed by both parties; out-of-hours return procedures and pickup location opening hours are stated.

sources.title: Leaseurope Guidelines to the Code of Best Practice for the Car and Van Short Term Hire Industry
sources.notes: Conciliation-service guidelines to the short-term hire code: mandatory charges in the headline price; fuel policies prominently highlighted during booking with return at the same fuel level at no extra charge; the damage-dispute procedure disclosed during booking with the right to challenge, photographic evidence encouraged, and evidence plus repair-cost calculation provided for any charge; pre-authorisations and deposits stated during booking and refunded or unblocked as soon as possible after the rental.

sources.title: Recipe app design examples
sources.notes: Cooking mode for divided attention and messy hands: one large readable step at a time with visible progress and previous and next controls, quantities in the instruction or one tap away, multiple labelled timers, screen kept awake with clear benefit, step and timer state persisted locally and reconciled after backgrounding, voice actions confirmed for destructive timer or step changes with a touch fallback.

sources.title: Drive-through guidelines for customers with disabilities
sources.notes: City disability office guidance on serving customers with disabilities at a drive-through: greet and take orders from customers with disabilities as from any other customer; a printed menu at the drive-through window and at interior registers on request; pen and paper available at drive-through windows; patience, since communication takes time; staff training on serving customers with disabilities.

sources.title: Complete multiple tasks pattern
sources.notes: Government design-system guidance for longer transactions: only use a complete-multiple-tasks page where tasks may be completed over several sessions; allow saving progress and continuing where the person left off; group related tasks and show their state.

sources.title: Task list component
sources.notes: Government design-system guidance on task lists for multi-step transactions: show each task with its state so the person can see what is done and what remains.

sources.title: Check answers pattern
sources.notes: Government design-system guidance: let people check their answers before submitting information to a service, with each answer changeable in place.

sources.title: How a customer applies for a passport online
sources.notes: Passport-office operational guidance: applicants complete and submit the application online, upload a digital photo, and pay the fee; the service states what documents are needed and how and when they are returned; the customer can track progress through submission, identity confirmation, and referee stages.

sources.title: Renew a passport online
sources.notes: National passport authority renewal page: pay the fee by card; the current document is cancelled when the renewal is submitted and cannot be used for travel afterwards; email status updates as the application moves through processing, approval, and dispatch, with a route to supply more information where asked.

sources.title: Mortgage Rule Review Instrument 2025
sources.notes: Financial-regulator rulebook instrument amending the mortgages conduct-of-business sourcebook: firms must assess affordability under the consumer duty and their own responsible-lending policy, including a modified affordability assessment for remortgaging.

sources.title: Consumer Protection Code: mortgage application timelines and refusal reasons
sources.notes: Financial-regulator consumer protection code: acknowledge a complete mortgage application within 3 working days, an incomplete one within 3 working days naming the documents still needed, and give the decision within 10 working days of receiving all documents or give reasons and an expected timeframe; give refusal reasons in writing within 10 working days of request.

sources.title: How to apply for a mortgage
sources.notes: Government-backed money-guidance service: affordability checks take regular household bills and spending into account and stress-test whether repayments stay affordable if rates rise; documents to collect include payslips, bank statements, identity and address proof, and proof of deposit.

sources.title: Manage fall detection on a smartwatch
sources.notes: Platform support documentation: where a hard fall is detected and the wearer is immobile for about a minute, a 30-second countdown begins with a wrist tap and a rising alarm; tapping cancel stops the call, and when the countdown ends the watch contacts emergency services on its own; where the wearer is moving, it waits for a response and never calls on its own; manual SOS is press-and-hold the side button, released to cancel; not all falls are detected.

sources.title: Fall detection on a smartwatch
sources.notes: Platform support documentation: when a hard fall is detected the watch waits about 30 seconds, then vibrates, rings loudly and asks whether to call emergency services; with no response it alarms and then calls after 60 seconds with an automated voice message; manual SOS is press the crown five times, then touch and hold the screen for three seconds, releasing the hold cancels the call; fall detection cannot detect all falls and needs a connection to call.

sources.title: Electronic Fund Transfer Act: disclosure of fees at automated teller machines
sources.notes: Consumer-protection regulator rule text: an operator imposing a fee at a machine must give notice disclosing the amount of the fee on the screen or on paper before the person is committed to paying it; a fee may be imposed only where the person elects to continue after receiving the notice.

sources.title: Disclosure of commission on payments via ATMs and payment terminals
sources.notes: Central bank and competition authority joint letter: disclose the commission amount charged on payments via machines before money is inserted, displayed on screen in a simple and easy-to-understand manner in clear legible type, and warn in advance whether money already inserted can be returned before final confirmation.

sources.title: Electronic fund transfers: receipts at electronic terminals
sources.notes: State regulator rule: receipts at electronic terminals must include a transfer identification number and a 24-hour toll-free telephone number for inquiries or complaints.

sources.title: Smart metering implementation programme: in-home display minimum requirements
sources.notes: Energy-regulator programme document (2010 consultation proposals): proposed minimum requirements for an in-home display include real-time use, historical use so the current period can be compared with a previous one, use shown in money as well as in units, and a visual marker for high and low use alongside the figures; verify against the current metering specification before relying on it for a published row.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.notes: Accessibility standard, Recommendation of 5 October 2023: adds nine success criteria since the previous version, six at Level A or AA, including a single-pointer alternative for dragging movements, help that stays in the same relative order across pages, no repeated entry of the same information in one process, and sign-in that does not depend on remembering a password or solving a puzzle.

sources.title: Interaction design patterns for augmented reality fitting rooms
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed paper proposing nine interaction patterns for fitting rooms that overlay garments on the person in a mirror or on a phone: separate catalogue and fitting steps, measurement with privacy, mid-air gestures kept low and brief, a touch or phone route for people unfamiliar with gestures, and a focus-group evaluation.

sources.title: The impact of information layout and auxiliary instruction display mode on the usability of virtual fitting interaction interfaces
sources.notes: Experiment with 60 participants: a grid layout served multi-item choice better than list or horizontal strips, and dark-on-light instruction text served single-item search and demanding tasks better; the grid with dark-on-light text was the fastest combination.

sources.title: The role of digital tools designed to help workers clearly and personally visualize their pension situation: the case of individual pension dashboards
sources.notes: Analysis of six national pension dashboards (Denmark, Sweden, Belgium, United Kingdom, Chile, Mexico) based on OECD data: integrate all income sources, use inflation-adjusted projections, present information in layers (total and projection first, breakdown by source second, plan detail third), offer dynamic calculators with optimistic, neutral and pessimistic scenarios, and help locate lost accounts.

sources.title: How to apply for a visa to come to the UK
sources.notes: Government guidance for visa applications: biometrics by appointment at a visa application centre within a stated window, a decision usually within 3 to 12 weeks depending on the visa, and travel not to be booked until the decision arrives.

sources.title: Ask for a visa administrative review
sources.notes: Government guidance on challenging a visa decision: the decision letter states whether an administrative review can be asked for, with eligibility, time limits, and the review process.

sources.title: Application for Schengen visa
sources.notes: Harmonised visa application form under the Visa Code: main purpose of the journey, duration of the intended stay, and intended dates of arrival and departure.

sources.title: Popular questions
sources.notes: Government help pages for visa applicants: biometrics at a contracted collection centre where needed, published processing times, and refusal notices that state review rights and how to appeal.

sources.title: Pay the Dartford Crossing charge (Dart Charge)
sources.notes: Government guidance for paying a penalty charge notice: only the vehicle registration number and the notice reference number are needed; no account is required.

sources.title: Parking tickets
sources.notes: Council guidance for paying a penalty charge notice by its number and the vehicle registration, and for challenging it: paying the notice counts as an admission of liability, so a challenge is not accepted after payment.

sources.title: Pay or challenge your parking fine ticket
sources.notes: Council guidance: payment and challenge cannot happen together; paying closes any open challenge.

sources.title: Do Not Rely on Users Calculations or Memorizing Information
sources.notes: Standards-body cognitive-accessibility pattern: pause between each option, wait for a slow speaker, listen for a quiet or hesitant speaker, use simple one-word responses, and state the option before the number.

sources.title: Provide Human Help
sources.notes: Standards-body cognitive-accessibility pattern: human help must never require managing a complex voice menu; a number going directly to a human, for example by pressing 0.

sources.title: Access to Cash: Requirements for ATM Operators (Consultation Paper 164)
sources.notes: Regulator consultation paper (December 2025, proposed requirements): cash machines stocked with at least two denominations, one below 50 in local currency, and receipts provided at the request of the user with prescribed contents; consultation open until March 2026, so the requirements are proposed rather than final.

sources.title: Choosing childcare
sources.notes: Government guidance on choosing childcare: visit at least two or three settings while children are being looked after, and make a second visit where there are misgivings; childcare needs follow working hours and shift patterns.

sources.title: Your childcare options
sources.notes: Public information service guidance on childcare choices: the child's age is among the first factors to consider, alongside full-time or part-time need and the hours required; visit providers while children are present.

sources.title: Risk Management of Remote Deposit Capture
sources.notes: Regulator guidance (issued January 2009; regulator copy revised June 2026): remote deposit capture risks from the point of capture include poor image quality and inaccurate electronic data; original items are retained by the customer with document management procedures until destruction or voiding; items can be endorsed, franked, or otherwise noted as already processed to prevent re-processing; contracts should establish cut-off times and state how the customer knows the deposit was accepted.

sources.title: ENERGY STAR Product Specification for Smart Home Energy Management Systems, Version 1.0
sources.notes: Programme specification for home energy management systems: the interface must show energy use by device across time intervals of a day or less, with daily, weekly, monthly or annual performance and comparison with previous periods; packages must include a smart power strip, smart plugs, or a home energy sub-metering system, with load devices reporting their energy use; a user notification process is required where detection fails, and time-of-use pricing must be usable to manage energy costs.

sources.title: A design-oriented framework for smart home energy management system interfaces to support energy-saving occupant behavior
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed conference paper (2026): a design framework for home energy management interfaces grounded in five core functions - information delivery, real-time feedback, personal motivation, control flexibility, and social comparison - yielding thirty actionable design guidelines and a five-function prototype.

sources.title: How to Offer Curbside Pickup: Retail Guide (2026)
sources.notes: Platform guide to curbside pickup: order placed ahead and paid online, pickup in a designated area with numbered spaces, phone or text arrival instructions, expected pickup time shown at checkout, ready-for-pickup notification, and arrival detection through a tap, geofencing, or the car's display, with live pickup status after arrival.

sources.title: CX principles for online applications
sources.notes: Government guidance for online benefit applications: plain-language questions, conditional questions that show only what applies, contextual help beside the question, progress shown and saved at every step, and equitable access for people with disabilities, limited English, and people under stress.

sources.title: Benefits Enrollment Application
sources.notes: Prototype and design principles for user-centred benefits enrolment: real-time eligibility determination and same-day enrolment, few steps to the programmes wanted, mobile-first design, plain language, fewer prompts per screen, and applications personalised to the applicant.

sources.title: Our Top Three Tips for Improving Online Benefits Applications
sources.notes: Human-centred benefits application guidance: a welcoming front door in the applicant's preferred language, no account creation before starting, one application covering several programmes, and document upload after submission; a redesigned integrated application cut the time to apply for several benefits from over an hour to under 15 minutes.

sources.title: Designing with empathy
sources.notes: Benefit finder organised by life event rather than programme name: a short plain-language eligibility form, fewer words and shorter sentences, mobile-first, usable with or without assistive technology, completable in a few minutes.

sources.title: An 'interface first' bureaucracy: Interface design, Universal Credit and the digital welfare state
sources.notes: Peer-reviewed analysis of how interfaces mediate access to public benefits: a five-fold typology of interface design elements in the benefits context — structuring data input, interaction architecture, operative controls, prompting and priming, and integrations.
